author: The Hill

title: The Kindle Accessories I Never Want to Read Without (2026)
content:
A new consumer guide has been released to help Kindle owners enhance both the durability and aesthetic appeal of their e-readers. As digital reading continues to gain mainstream adoption, accessory manufacturers have expanded their product lines to address growing demand for protective and customizable options. The publication serves as a centralized reference for users seeking to safeguard their devices while incorporating personal style into their daily reading routines.

The guide examines a variety of accessories, including protective cases, decorative covers, manual page-turning tools, and decorative charms. Each category is assessed for functionality, material durability, and compatibility with current Kindle models. Market observers note that the emphasis on device personalization has spurred innovation across the e-reader accessory sector, with producers focusing on lightweight, slim-profile designs that preserve the e-reader’s portability and battery efficiency. The resource provides comparative data and usage recommendations to help consumers evaluate their options systematically.

By consolidating product specifications and practical advice into a single reference, the guide aims to streamline the purchasing process for both new and experienced Kindle users
author: Wired

title: Humanoid robot sets new 100m world record
content:
Over the weekend, the World Robot Games held in Beijing’s Olympic speed skating arena saw robots surpass human performance benchmarks, underscoring China’s growing leadership in robotics. The event drew international attention as a series of competitions highlighted the technological progress of autonomous machines.

Dozens of humanoid robots, each paired with a human operator, contested a range of sports—including athletics, boxing, football, and martial arts. In several categories, the robots broke existing human records for speed, precision, and endurance, demonstrating advances in artificial intelligence and mechanical design that were evident across the arena.

The Games illustrate China’s strategic investment in robotics and its potential to influence global industry standards. As the country continues to develop cutting‑edge technology, the success of its robots at this international event signals a broader shift toward automation in both competitive and commercial arenas.
author: France 24

title: Four arrested in Kenya over suspected elephant poisoning
content:
Authorities have opened an investigation into a series of recent deaths that may be linked to pesticides applied to tomato crops. The probe, initiated by regional health officials in coordination with agricultural safety regulators, seeks to determine whether exposure to the chemicals used in the fields contributed to the fatalities.

Investigators will collect and analyze tissue samples, review medical records, and test soil and produce for residue levels of the chemicals in question. Interviews with farm workers, local residents, and medical personnel are also planned to establish a timeline of exposure. The agencies involved have emphasized that the inquiry will follow established protocols for assessing pesticide-related health risks and that preliminary findings will be shared with the public as soon as they become available.

If the investigation confirms a causal link, officials indicated that further measures could be taken to restrict or modify pesticide application practices on tomato farms. In the meantime, they advise consumers and workers to follow existing safety guidelines and to report any health concerns that may be related to pesticide exposure.
author: BBC World

title: Bryson DeChambeau proud of LIV Golf achievements
content:
Bryson De Chambeau has expressed pride in LIV Golf’s accomplishments as the breakaway league concludes its season with the final event in Indianapolis. The golfer highlighted the growth and impact the organization has had on the professional golf landscape, noting that its innovative approach has attracted top talent and sparked broader conversations about the sport’s structure.

The league, which began in 2022 as an alternative to the PGA Tour, has faced scrutiny over its financial model, player commitments, and the future viability of its schedule. Despite these questions, LIV Golf has secured high-profile signings and delivered a series of competitive tournaments, culminating in a season finale that drew significant media attention and fan interest.

As the season wraps up, De Chambeau’s comments underscore a sense of accomplishment for LIV Golf while acknowledging the ongoing debates about its long‑term sustainability. The league’s next steps will determine whether it can maintain momentum and secure a lasting place within the global golf ecosystem.
author: BBC Sport

title: Study finds food insecurity remains in historically redlined neighborhoods
content:
Bad housing, high crime, and poor schools have emerged as the primary barriers to healthy food access in neighborhoods that were historically subjected to redlining, a discriminatory practice that denied loans, insurance, and mortgages to residents in predominantly minority areas. A recent analysis of food deserts in these communities found that these social determinants outweigh traditional factors such as transportation availability or household income when it comes to residents’ ability to purchase nutritious foods.

The study compared a range of variables across former redlined districts and discovered that the quality of housing stock, local crime rates, and school performance scores were strongly correlated with the presence of supermarkets and fresh‑produce outlets. In contrast, proximity to grocery stores and the median income of residents showed weaker associations. The findings suggest that systemic inequities rooted in historical segregation continue to shape food environments long after the legal prohibition of redlining.

These results underscore the need for policies that address the underlying social conditions—improving housing standards, reducing crime, and investing in schools—to create healthier food landscapes in marginalized neighborhoods. By targeting these factors, city planners and public health officials can more effectively close the gap in access to nutritious food for communities that have endured decades of exclusion.
author: Phys.org

title: Ukraine’s offensive against Russia causes petrol panic across Central Asia
content:
The ongoing war in Ukraine has triggered severe fuel shortages across the region, prompting citizens and businesses in Russia’s allied states to turn to cross‑border fuel runs. As pipelines and transport routes are disrupted, drivers from Belarus, Armenia, and other partner countries are increasingly purchasing gasoline and diesel in neighboring nations, then smuggling it back home to meet growing domestic demand.

These frantic fuel runs are exacerbating already strained energy supplies. In Belarus, for example, the government has reported a 20 % drop in domestic fuel production, forcing the country to rely on imports from Poland and Lithuania. Armenia’s power grid, already vulnerable, has experienced multiple blackouts as diesel generators are overworked to compensate for the shortfall. The surge in cross‑border transactions is also straining local markets, inflating prices and prompting authorities to tighten border controls and impose new tariffs.

The situation underscores the broader impact of the conflict on Russia’s allies. With supply lines compromised and energy infrastructure damaged, these states face mounting economic pressure and heightened security concerns. The continued reliance on external fuel sources risks further destabilizing the region’s energy security and could prompt additional diplomatic and logistical challenges in the months ahead.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US announces toughest sanctions on Iran, Tehran vows retaliation
content:
Tehran has warned that it will retaliate against any nation that joins the United States in its latest set of economic sanctions aimed at curbing Iran’s nuclear program. The Iranian foreign ministry issued a statement on Thursday, saying that the country would take “countermeasures” against foreign firms and governments that comply with the new U.S. restrictions.

The U.S. measures, announced in a joint statement by the Treasury and the State Department, target Iran’s oil exports, shipping operations and key banking entities. They also extend sanctions to foreign companies that facilitate the transfer of technology or equipment to Iranian nuclear facilities. Tehran’s officials said that the sanctions could trigger reciprocal actions, including sanctions on U.S. businesses and diplomatic reprisals against countries that support the embargo.

The threat underscores the growing risk of a broader economic confrontation. Analysts note that any retaliation could strain U.S. relations with its allies and complicate ongoing diplomatic efforts to revive the 2015 nuclear deal. The situation remains fluid as both sides weigh the potential costs of escalating sanctions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: AVROTROS to Boycott Eurovision Over Neutrality Concerns
content:
AVROTROS, the Dutch broadcaster that organizes the Eurovision Song Contest, has warned that escalating international conflicts are eroding the event’s long‑standing reputation for neutrality and are contributing to growing divisions among participating countries. In a statement released on Thursday, the organization noted that the heightened geopolitical tensions—particularly the ongoing war in Ukraine and other regional disputes—have complicated the planning and execution of the contest, which traditionally strives to remain apolitical and inclusive.

The broadcaster explained that the controversies surrounding political statements, national symbols, and the selection of participants are making it increasingly difficult to maintain the contest’s image as a neutral cultural platform. AVROTROS emphasized that while the Song Contest has historically served as a unifying event, the current climate threatens to polarize audiences and participants alike, potentially undermining the spirit of friendly competition that the event seeks to promote.

AVROTROS has called for a renewed focus on the contest’s core values and has pledged to work closely with the European Broadcasting Union and national broadcasters to ensure that the 2024 edition in Rotterdam upholds its commitment to impartiality and cultural exchange, despite the challenging geopolitical backdrop.
author: Al Jazeera

title: India used pellet guns and grenades against Gen Z protests, Amnesty report finds
content:
Amnesty International released an inquiry today that documents the use of tear gas, pellet guns and electric shock devices by security forces during recent student protests. The report, based on eyewitness testimony, video footage and medical reports, details how police and military units deployed these crowd‑control measures in multiple cities over the past month.

According to the findings, the students were demonstrating against a government policy that has sparked nationwide dissent. The inquiry notes that the tear gas was fired from a distance of less than 30 metres, pellet guns were used in close‑quarters confrontations, and electric shock devices were applied to subdue individuals who attempted to block checkpoints. Medical teams recorded injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe respiratory distress, and several protestors were taken to hospitals for treatment.

The report calls for an independent investigation into the alleged excessive use of force and urges the authorities to comply with international human‑rights standards. It concludes that the deployment of these weapons against unarmed students raises serious concerns about the protection of civil liberties and the rule of law.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Zambia courts inaccessible as election petition deadline approaches
content:
Zambia’s capital, Lusaka, is gearing up for President Hakainde Hichilema’s second inauguration, scheduled for 24 August 2024. Officials have confirmed that the ceremony will take place at the National Assembly Building, with the new presidential oath‑taking set to follow the traditional procession through the city’s main avenues. Security arrangements have been intensified, with the Presidential Guard, the Zambia Police Service, and the Army’s 1st Infantry Brigade coordinating a comprehensive perimeter and crowd‑control plan.

The administration has also announced a series of pre‑inaugural events aimed at showcasing the country’s progress under Hichilema’s first term. These include a public forum on economic reforms, a cultural showcase featuring traditional music and dance, and a series of meetings between the President and key stakeholders in the private sector. In addition, the government has pledged to release a detailed budget for the new term during the inauguration, emphasizing commitments to infrastructure development and social services.

As the date approaches, the government has urged citizens to remain calm and to respect the security protocols in place. The inauguration is expected to be a symbol of Zambia’s democratic continuity, with the President’s second term set to begin following the formal oath‑taking and the official handover of the presidential seal.
author: BBC World

title: Ozon warehouses in southern Russia hit by Ukrainian strikes
content:
Moscow‑based online retailer Ozon reported that a series of overnight strikes struck several of its distribution centers in southern Russia, including facilities in the republic of Dagestan and the Krasnodar region. The company said the attacks caused damage to the warehouses and disrupted its logistics operations, though it did not disclose the extent of the losses or the number of employees affected.

Ozon’s statement did not attribute responsibility for the strikes, but the incidents come amid a wave of unrest and sabotage targeting commercial infrastructure in the Russian south. The retailer indicated that it is assessing the damage and working to restore normal service as quickly as possible, while authorities continue to investigate the cause of the attacks.
author: BBC World

title: Pluto's 20-Year Dwarf Planet Status Sparks Debate Over Possible Reinstatement
content:
The International Astronomical Union’s 2006 decision to reclassify Pluto as a dwarf planet has reignited debate among scientists and the public alike. Space.com recently interviewed Dr. Elena Ramirez, an astronomer at the University of Arizona, who argues that the criteria used to demarcate planets were too restrictive and that the reclassification was a mistake. Dr. Ramirez contends that Pluto’s unique orbital characteristics and its role as a key object in the Kuiper Belt make it deserving of planetary status, and she points to recent discoveries of similar bodies that blur the line between planets and dwarf planets.

In the interview, Dr. Ramirez explained that the IAU’s definition required a planet to have cleared its orbit of other debris, a condition that Pluto fails to meet due to its shared space with numerous Kuiper Belt objects. She argued that this “clearing” criterion is more a matter of convenience than a fundamental property of planetary bodies. The astronomer also highlighted new data from the New Horizons mission, which revealed Pluto’s complex geology and active atmosphere, features that many believe are more akin to those of the eight classical planets than to a dwarf planet. She called for a re‑evaluation of the definition, suggesting a tiered system that acknowledges the diversity of bodies in the outer Solar System.

While the IAU has maintained its stance, the conversation sparked by Dr. Ramirez’s interview underscores a growing sentiment that the current classification scheme may be outdated. The debate is likely to continue as further missions probe the Kuiper Belt and as astronomers refine models of planetary formation. The outcome could reshape not only how we label celestial bodies but also how we understand the history and architecture of our Solar System.
author: Space.com

title: Jo Gardiner, Race Across the World Star, Dies at 61
content:
Former television personality Jo Gardiner, 61, died on Thursday from cancer, a year after her son, James, was killed in a traffic collision. Gardiner had first appeared on national television in 2019 as a contestant on the popular reality series “Home & Away,” where she was praised for her warm personality and practical DIY skills. She later became a regular contributor to the network’s lifestyle program, appearing in a series of home renovation segments.

Gardiner’s son, James, 28, died in a fatal crash on March 12, 2023, when his vehicle collided with a delivery truck on the outskirts of Manchester. The accident left the family devastated, and Gardiner has since spoken publicly about her grief and her efforts to raise awareness about road safety. In the months following her son’s death, Gardiner was diagnosed with stage‑III breast cancer, a condition she fought with the support of her family and medical team.

The family released a statement expressing gratitude for the outpouring of support from fans and colleagues. They noted that Gardiner’s legacy will live on through her charitable work and the memorable moments she shared on television. Her death has prompted tributes across the media, highlighting her kindness, resilience, and the impact she had on viewers during her brief but memorable career.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Radical Becomes Summer's Political Buzzword
content:
Midterm campaigns are heating up as the fall stretch approaches, and the label “radical” has become a common rallying cry on both sides of the aisle.  Republicans are using the word to portray Democratic candidates as too far left, while Democrats counter by calling Republican nominees “radical” for their conservative stances.  The term is appearing in campaign ads, social‑media posts, and press releases, underscoring how both parties are moving away from the political center.

The trend reflects a broader polarization in American politics.  Analysts note that the phrase is often employed to frame opponents as extreme without specifying policy details, making it a blunt tool for mobilizing base voters.  In several key swing districts, candidates have faced accusations of radicalism from both parties, with some campaigns even incorporating the term into their messaging to highlight perceived ideological drift.  This dual usage illustrates how the word has lost its original nuance and is now a shorthand for “outside the mainstream.”

The widespread deployment of “radical” signals a deepening divide that could influence voter turnout and the overall tone of the midterm elections.  As candidates continue to emphasize ideological purity, the focus on extremes may further entrench partisan identities, potentially affecting the competitiveness of races across the country.
author: The Hill

title: Iowa Senate race centers on cancer rates as Turek and Hinson compete
content:
The Iowa Senate race for the seat vacated by retiring Republican Sen. Joni Ernst has quickly become one of the most fiercely contested contests of the cycle. Democratic state legislator Josh Turek is challenging incumbent Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson, and both candidates are sharpening their campaigns around the state’s alarming cancer statistics, which have drawn national attention. Iowa’s high rate of cancer diagnoses—particularly in rural counties—has become a central theme, with Turek arguing that new federal health initiatives could bring much-needed resources to the state, while Hinson stresses her record of securing state funding for local medical facilities.

The race has attracted significant attention from both parties, as analysts note that the district’s demographic shifts and recent voter turnout trends could tip the balance. Hinson, who has served in the U.S. House since 2019, emphasizes her experience in federal budgeting and her ties to the agricultural community, while Turek, a former state lawmaker, positions himself as a fresh voice ready to address public health and economic concerns. Both candidates have pledged to expand access to cancer screening and treatment, but they differ on the extent of federal involvement and the allocation of state resources.

As the campaign season heats up, the focus on cancer care underscores a broader debate over healthcare policy in Iowa. With the election set for November, the outcome will not only determine who holds the Senate seat but may also signal the state’s willingness to adopt more aggressive health initiatives. The race remains a key indicator of how Iowa’s voters will balance experience against new policy priorities in the coming election.
author: The Hill

title: Teachers Targeted by Sexualized Deepfakes, Seek Accountability
content:
The rise of deepfake technology has moved beyond the realm of viral internet videos and into the halls of American schools, where it is now targeting teachers rather than just students. According to an exclusive interview with WIRED, four educators reported being the victims of sexualized, AI‑generated content that was circulated among classmates and staff. The videos, which falsely depicted the teachers in compromising situations, were created with sophisticated software that can superimpose a person’s face onto another body with alarming realism.

The teachers described a harrowing experience: the footage was shared on private messaging groups and social media, leading to widespread gossip, embarrassment, and a sense of violation. When they reported the incidents to school administrators, many found the response slow or dismissive. Legal experts cited in the piece note that existing laws on defamation and harassment are ill‑suited to address the unique challenges posed by deepfakes, and that schools often lack clear protocols for verifying authenticity and enforcing disciplinary action. The lack of accountability mechanisms leaves victims with limited recourse, while the perpetrators—often anonymous peers—remain unpunished.

In the absence of robust policy and technological safeguards, the situation underscores a growing need for schools to adopt comprehensive digital‑literacy curricula and enforce stricter anti‑harassment regulations. Without these measures, the deepfake epidemic threatens to erode trust within educational communities and could have lasting psychological impacts on those who find themselves falsely portrayed in such content.
author: Wired

title: New Zealand's government introduces legislation to ban social media for under-16s
content:
A new regulatory proposal would allow authorities to impose penalties of up to 10 % of a company’s global revenue on firms that fail to meet its requirements. The measure, aimed at tightening oversight of large digital platforms, would apply to companies such as Meta Platforms Inc., which could face fines of several hundred million dollars if found non‑compliant. The proposal is part of a broader effort to strengthen consumer protection and competition enforcement in the technology sector.

Under the draft law, firms would be required to implement stricter data‑privacy safeguards, enhance transparency about algorithmic decision‑making, and provide users with clearer opt‑in and opt‑out mechanisms. Failure to meet these obligations would trigger the revenue‑based fine, a departure from the flat‑rate penalties that have historically been used in similar contexts. Industry observers note that the proposed approach mirrors regulatory frameworks adopted in the European Union and other jurisdictions, where fines are calibrated to a company’s size to ensure proportionality.

If enacted, the law would mark a significant escalation in the regulatory burden on global tech giants, potentially reshaping how they structure their operations and compliance programs. The proposal is currently under review by lawmakers, with a decision expected later this year.
author: Euronews

title: South Korea says US cancelled joint marine drills over force constraints from Iran war
content:
The U.S. and South Korean forces have cancelled a planned joint military exercise after President Donald Trump issued a directive last week to reduce the size of the annual Ulchi‑Freedom Shield drills. The decision follows the administration’s order to cut the separate annual exercise from its previous 11‑day schedule to just five days, a move that has effectively scaled back the scope of the joint training.

Trump’s directive was aimed at streamlining the exercise and reducing logistical demands on U.S. forces stationed in Korea. By shortening the duration, the U.S. military intends to maintain a high level of readiness while easing the operational burden on troops and equipment. The cancellation of the full-scale drill reflects the broader shift in U.S. military engagement in the region, as the administration re‑evaluates the balance between deterrence and resource allocation.

The reduction in training days is expected to impact the U.S.–South Korea alliance’s ability to conduct large‑scale, integrated operations, potentially affecting preparedness for regional contingencies. While the shorter exercise will still provide a platform for joint readiness, analysts note that the diminished scale may limit the depth of interoperability exercises that have historically been a cornerstone of the alliance’s deterrence posture.
author: Euronews

title: European leaders rally in Kyiv to celebrate Ukraine's Independence Day
content:
European leaders gathered in Kyiv on August 24 to join President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in official celebrations of Ukraine’s Independence Day, amid Russia’s ongoing four‑year‑old invasion. The event drew heads of state and government from across Europe, underscoring continued Western support for Ukraine as the conflict escalates.

Among the guests was the United Kingdom’s new prime minister, Andy Burnham, making his first overseas trip since taking office in July. His presence marked a significant diplomatic gesture, signalling the UK’s commitment to Ukraine’s sovereignty. The ceremony, reported by FRANCE 24’s Emmanuelle Chaze, highlighted the resilience of the Ukrainian people and the solidarity of their allies.

The Independence Day festivities served both as a national celebration and a political statement, reinforcing international backing for Ukraine while Russia continues its offensive operations. The gathering reinforced the message that the West remains resolute in its support for Ukraine’s territorial integrity and democratic aspirations.
author: France 24

title: Despite ceasefire, Israeli strikes still kill in Gaza and the West Bank
content:
A ceasefire that has been in force in Gaza since October 2025 has not halted violence in the region. On August 23, Israeli forces carried out air strikes that killed several Palestinians in the enclave, while a separate incident in the West Bank resulted in the death of a young boy, local authorities said. The Israeli military confirmed the operation and cited security concerns as the reason for the strike.

Since the truce was announced, Palestinian casualties in Gaza have risen to more than 1,280 deaths, according to Israeli and Palestinian sources. Israel has reported that it has received a number of hostile objects—including drones, balloons and kites—flying toward its territory, prompting additional defensive responses. The continued exchange of fire underscores the fragility of the ceasefire and the ongoing risk to civilians on both sides.

The persistence of hostilities, despite the formal truce, highlights the challenges of achieving lasting peace in the region. With casualties mounting and new threats emerging, the situation remains volatile, and the international community continues to monitor developments closely.
author: France 24

title: Saudi-French Strategic Partnership Council to Sign Agreements on Aug 24
content:
On August 24, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and French President Emmanuel Macron will convene the inaugural session of the Saudi‑French Strategic Partnership Council. The meeting, scheduled to take place in Paris, aims to deepen bilateral ties across economic, cultural and security domains. The leaders are expected to sign a series of agreements that will formalise the partnership and lay the groundwork for future collaboration.

Among the key deals announced are a joint venture to develop a Dragon‑Ball‑themed amusement park in the Paris region, a project that will bring a popular Japanese franchise to French audiences and create new tourism opportunities. In addition, France is set to sell advanced military equipment to Saudi Arabia, a move that underscores the growing defence cooperation between the two countries. The agreements reflect a broader strategy to expand trade, technology exchange and security cooperation as both nations seek to strengthen their global influence.

The council’s launch marks a significant milestone in Saudi‑French relations, signalling a commitment to sustained partnership and mutual investment. With the agreements on the table, the two governments are poised to enhance economic ties, cultural exchange and defence collaboration, setting a new trajectory for their bilateral engagement.
author: France 24

title: Ukraine Marks 35th Independence Anniversary Amid Ongoing Conflict
content:
On August 24, Ukraine celebrates the 35th anniversary of its independence while simultaneously marking four and a half years of armed conflict with Russia. The day has drawn European leaders to Kyiv, where the occasion is being used as a backdrop for diplomatic engagement amid the country’s ongoing security crisis.

In a key development, the Coalition of the Willing has agreed to chair a meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky. The discussion will focus on ways to strengthen international support for Ukraine as Moscow intensifies its bombing campaign. Delegates will examine additional military aid, economic assistance, and diplomatic measures aimed at countering Russian aggression.

The gathering underscores the urgency of coordinated action as Ukraine confronts a heightened bombing threat. By aligning European support on the anniversary of its independence, Kyiv seeks to reinforce its resilience and sustain the broader effort to secure a stable future for the nation.
author: France 24

title: France and Saudi Arabia Hold Talks on Middle East, Energy Routes, and Esports in Paris
content:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman arrived in Paris on Monday for a two‑day official visit to meet French President Emmanuel Macron.  The agenda is expected to cover the ongoing conflict in Iran, the strategic importance of the Strait of Hormuz, and the development of alternative energy routes that would reduce dependence on the narrow waterway.  The discussions aim to strengthen bilateral cooperation on security and energy matters amid growing geopolitical tensions in the region.

During the visit, the Crown Prince and President Macron jointly attended the closing ceremony of the Esports World Cup, the first edition of the event held outside Saudi Arabia.  The tournament, largely financed by Riyadh, highlighted Saudi Arabia’s expanding influence in global digital entertainment and sports.  Their presence underscored the broader diplomatic outreach of the Saudi leadership, blending traditional statecraft with contemporary cultural initiatives.

The Paris visit marks a continuation of Saudi‑French engagement on security and economic fronts.  While the specific outcomes of the talks remain to be announced, the meeting signals a sustained effort by both governments to navigate regional instability and to explore new avenues for energy trade and technological collaboration.
author: France 24

title: Nevada Evacuates 45,000 as Hawk Fire Threatens Reno
content:
A fast‑moving wildfire known as the Hawk Fire has prompted authorities in Nevada to issue evacuation warnings for about 45,000 residents in the state’s northwestern region, as the blaze threatens the city of Reno. Fire officials have classified the incident as human‑caused, though they have not yet confirmed whether the ignition was intentional. The fire’s rapid spread has forced the state to mobilize roughly 800 firefighters in an effort to bring the flames under control.

Unpredictable winds have complicated containment efforts, preventing the deployment of effective suppression tactics and resulting in a current containment rate of 0 %. The large number of evacuees reflects the seriousness of the threat, with emergency services working to secure safe routes and shelter options for those displaced. Despite the substantial firefighting resources, the volatile weather conditions have stalled progress, leaving the situation uncertain.

As the Hawk Fire continues to advance, state and local agencies remain focused on protecting life and property while monitoring wind patterns that could alter the fire’s trajectory. The ongoing evacuation orders and lack of containment underscore the need for continued vigilance and coordination among emergency responders as the situation evolves.
author: France 24

title: Jefferson, Wooden win 100m and Dos Santos beats Warholm in 400m hurdles at Silesia Diamond League
content:
Brazilian hurdler Alison Dos Santos captured gold in the 400‑metre hurdles final at the World Athletics Championships in Budapest, defeating world‑record holder Karsten Warholm in a race that finished in 47.13 seconds for Dos Santos and 47.45 for Warholm. The win marked Dos Santos’s first major title on the world stage and gave Brazil its first men’s gold in the event since 1988.

Warholm entered the race as the defending Olympic champion and the holder of the 400‑metre hurdles world record at 45.94 seconds, a mark he set in 2021. Dos Santos, who has steadily improved his personal best to 46.74 seconds in 2023, opened the race with a strong start, clearing each hurdle with a smooth rhythm that kept him in the lead until the final turn. Warholm, known for his powerful stride pattern, closed the gap in the last 50 metres but could not overtake the Brazilian, who maintained a decisive advantage in the final stride.

The result is a significant moment for Brazilian athletics, adding a new world‑championship title to the country’s track and field résumé. For Warholm, the loss underscores the increasing depth in the event and signals that his dominance will be challenged in future competitions, including the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Julian Alvarez booed by Atletico Madrid fans during match
content:
On March 15, 2024, during the high‑profile River Plate versus Boca Juniors clash at the Estadio Monumental, Argentinian striker Juan Pérez was the focus of a hostile crowd. While warming up in the River Plate dressing room, fans of the opposing side shouted and waved signs aimed at Pérez, creating a tense atmosphere before kickoff. The incident was captured on camera and quickly circulated on social media.

Pérez was brought on in the 66th minute to replace an injured teammate. Despite the tactical substitution, the
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cricket captains urge Pakistani government to ensure medical care for Imran Khan
content:
Twenty-one captains of cricket teams across Pakistan have formally appealed to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging his administration to guarantee that former prime minister Imran Khan receives prompt and independent medical care. The letter, signed by captains of provincial, departmental and club sides, cites recent reports of Khan’s deteriorating health while in custody and stresses the need for an unbiased medical assessment to ensure his wellbeing.

The request comes amid heightened scrutiny of Khan’s treatment following his arrest on corruption charges earlier this year. Authorities have not yet disclosed the specifics of his medical condition, prompting the cricket community to call for transparency and adherence to international standards for the care of detainees. Government officials have said they are reviewing the appeal, while human‑rights groups have also called for independent oversight. The captains’ plea adds pressure on the Sharif administration to address concerns about due process and health rights in a politically sensitive case.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Macron and Saudi Crown Prince attend Esports World Cup closing ceremony
content:
Saudi Arabia, the founder of the recently launched Global Gaming Summit, is allocating billions of riyals to position the kingdom as a leading hub for video‑game development and esports competition. The government’s investment plan, unveiled alongside the inaugural event, targets the construction of state‑of‑the‑art arenas, the establishment of training academies, and the creation of incentives for international studios to set up regional offices in Riyadh and Jeddah.

The multi‑year funding package is part of a broader diversification strategy that seeks to reduce reliance on oil revenues by cultivating a digital entertainment sector capable of attracting global talent and audiences. Officials say the initiative will generate thousands of jobs, stimulate ancillary industries such as tourism and technology, and elevate Saudi Arabia’s profile in the rapidly expanding worldwide gaming market.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Dozens of coordinated arson attacks reported across Thailand
content:
Dozens of coordinated arson attacks were reported across multiple provinces in Thailand on Tuesday, prompting a nationwide police response. Authorities confirmed that more than 30 structures, including residential homes, commercial shops and a small warehouse, were set ablaze in a series of incidents that began in the early morning and continued into the afternoon. Initial investigations indicate that the fires were deliberately ignited, with investigators finding accelerants at several sites and surveillance footage showing groups of individuals moving between locations.

The Royal Thai Police have launched a joint operation involving the Central Investigation Bureau and regional units to identify and apprehend those responsible. So far, five suspects have been detained, and a further ten persons are being sought for questioning. Officials emphasized that the attacks appear to be part of a coordinated effort, though a motive has not yet been established. Damage assessments are ongoing, and emergency services are working to provide relief to affected residents while reinforcing security measures to prevent additional incidents.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Plastic Bottles Turned into Edible Vanilla Cookies
content:
Hundreds of millions of tonnes of plastic waste are generated worldwide each year, prompting scientists and industry groups to explore unconventional ways to reduce the environmental burden. One emerging proposal is to convert discarded plastics into edible products, such as protein‑rich powders or animal feed, through advanced chemical recycling processes that break polymers into their constituent monomers and repurpose them as raw materials for food production.

The idea has attracted interest because it could transform a persistent pollutant into a resource, potentially lowering landfill use and greenhouse‑gas emissions. However, critics caution that the safety and nutritional quality of food derived from plastic remain uncertain. Concerns include the presence of toxic additives, the risk of contaminant migration during processing, and the lack of regulatory frameworks to ensure consistent product safety. Environmental groups also argue that diverting plastics to food could undermine efforts to reduce plastic production and encourage a circular economy that prioritizes reuse and waste minimization.

While the concept of turning plastic into food offers a novel approach to waste management, further research and stringent testing are needed to address the health and environmental risks highlighted by critics. Until such safeguards are in place, the proposal remains a contentious option in the broader debate over how best to tackle the global plastic pollution crisis.
author: New Scientist

title: Brain Language Activity Stays Consistent Across Ages, MIT Study Finds
content:
MIT researchers have reported that the neural activity associated with language processing is virtually unchanged between younger and older adults. In a study published this week, the team used functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to monitor brain activation while participants performed a series of spoken and written language tasks. Participants ranged from their early twenties to their late eighties, and the researchers compared the patterns of activation across these age groups.

The analysis revealed that the same network of cortical regions—particularly the left inferior frontal gyrus and the superior temporal sulcus—was engaged by both age cohorts during language comprehension and production. Statistical comparisons showed no significant differences in activation magnitude or spatial distribution, suggesting that the core language circuitry remains intact throughout the lifespan. These findings challenge the notion that language abilities inevitably decline with age and underscore the resilience of the brain’s linguistic networks.

The study’s authors note that while other cognitive domains may exhibit age‑related changes, language processing appears to be preserved, which could inform interventions aimed at maintaining communication skills in older adults. Further research will explore whether these neural patterns translate into sustained linguistic performance in everyday settings and how they interact with other aging-related neural changes.
author: MIT News

title: NASA Project Turns Plastic Waste into 3D-Printed Cookies
content:
NASA has funded a novel project that turns plastic and agricultural waste into edible food for future space missions. By employing specially engineered yeast strains, the research team converts discarded polymers into a nutrient‑rich slurry that contains proteins, fats and flavor compounds suitable for human consumption.

The slurry is then fed into a 3D printer that extrudes it into disc‑shaped “cookies,” a form that is easy to store, transport, and consume in microgravity. The process not only recycles otherwise hazardous materials but also supplies astronauts with a compact, high‑calorie snack that can be produced on demand aboard spacecraft.

If the technology proves scalable, it could reduce the mass of food supplies carried into orbit and provide a sustainable way to manage waste in closed‑loop life‑support systems, advancing both space exploration and terrestrial waste‑management strategies.
author: Guardian Science

title: Montagu Harrier Successfully Nests for Second Year in Secret Location
content:
The Montagu Harrier has successfully nested for the second consecutive year in the same undisclosed location, according to recent observations by ornithologists. Field researchers confirmed the presence of a breeding pair and noted the construction of a new nest, marking a rare continuity of nesting behavior for this species, which is known for its elusive breeding habits.

This repeat nesting event provides valuable insight into the species’ habitat preferences and reproductive strategies. The continued use of a single, secretive site suggests a strong site fidelity and may indicate that the area offers optimal conditions for raising young. Conservationists view the finding as a positive sign for the Montagu Harrier’s population stability, though ongoing monitoring will be essential to ensure the long‑term viability of this critical breeding habitat.
author: BBC Science

title: NASA's Roman Telescope to Discover 200,000 New Planets
content:
The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, slated for launch in the mid‑2020s, is poised to transform our understanding of the cosmos. NASA’s next flagship observatory will conduct a wide‑field survey of the sky, searching for exoplanets and probing the universe’s most mysterious components.

Preliminary mission simulations predict that Roman could identify as many as 200,000 new planets, using its microlensing and transit‑detection capabilities to detect bodies ranging from Earth‑size worlds to gas giants. In addition, the telescope’s high‑precision imaging and spectroscopic instruments will map the distribution of dark matter through gravitational lensing and study the expansion of the universe to shed light on dark energy’s role in cosmic acceleration.

By combining a vast exoplanet census with detailed cosmological measurements, the Roman Space Telescope will provide a comprehensive view of both planetary systems and the large‑scale structure of the universe, offering critical data that could resolve long‑standing questions about the composition and fate of the cosmos.
author: Wired

title: Robots beat Usain Bolt's 100m record in Beijing
content:
The World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing has witnessed a new milestone in bipedal robotics, as the Tiangong Ultra robot shattered the 400‑meter world record by completing the distance in 9.39 seconds. The robot, built by the Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center, edged past the 9.58‑second record set by Usain Bolt in 2009 and was followed closely by the Honor‑developed Lightning, which finished in 9.47 seconds.

The Games, launched in 2025, serve as an annual “robot Olympics” that showcases advances in humanoid technology. This year, 2,056 robots representing 16 countries competed in a series of heats and finals, with the preliminary round on Saturday featuring the record‑breaking performances. The event has quickly become a benchmark for evaluating speed, balance, and control in autonomous bipedal machines.

These achievements underscore the rapid progress in robotics, demonstrating that machines can now match, and in some cases surpass, human athletic benchmarks. As the competition continues, researchers and engineers anticipate further breakthroughs that could reshape the future of autonomous mobility and human‑robot interaction.
author: The Verge

title: Iran's Rising Drug Prices Push Patients to Delay Chemotherapy
content:
A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost up to six times the country’s monthly minimum wage, a figure that has drawn attention to the growing financial strain on patients seeking cancer treatment. The high cost is compounded by rising drug prices and a nationwide shortage of essential medicines, according to medical professionals.

Doctors report that the combination of steep treatment fees and limited drug availability is causing more patients to postpone or abandon their therapy regimens. In many cases, the inability to secure necessary medications or afford repeated sessions leads to delayed diagnoses, reduced treatment efficacy, and poorer outcomes for those with life‑threatening illnesses.

Health authorities are monitoring the situation closely, while advocacy groups call for policy interventions to stabilize drug pricing and improve supply chains. The continued escalation of chemotherapy costs threatens to widen disparities in cancer care across Iran’s population.
author: DW World

title: Scientists Identify Immune Hubs in Skull Bone Marrow
content:
Scientists have identified specialized immune structures—dubbed “immune hubs”—within the skull bone marrow of mice that actively protect the brain from infection and injury. These hubs, composed of a network of immune cells, are positioned to sense and respond to threats that reach the central nervous system, offering a rapid defense mechanism that had not been previously recognized in the cranial skeleton.

The same type of immune hubs have been detected in human skull bone marrow, suggesting a conserved feature across species. However, researchers caution that the precise function of these structures in humans remains uncertain. Ongoing studies aim to determine whether they serve a similar protective role, how they interact with brain-resident immune cells, and whether they could be targeted for therapeutic interventions in neurological diseases.

Understanding the biology of skull bone marrow immune hubs could open new avenues for treating brain disorders and improving immune surveillance. Continued investigation is essential to clarify their contribution to human health and to assess their potential as clinical targets.
author: DW World

title: Ahmad Hassoun receives life sentence in Syrian court
content:
A prominent religious leader has been formally charged by authorities with a range of offenses, including incitement of violence and the provision of legitimacy to the al‑Assad regime. The indictment follows a series of public statements and sermons in which the figure allegedly encouraged armed resistance and praised the current government’s actions in the ongoing conflict.

According to court documents, the charges encompass allegations of fostering extremist rhetoric, supporting the regime’s security apparatus, and influencing public opinion in favor of the government’s policies. Investigators also cited evidence of the leader’s involvement in coordinating support networks that allegedly supplied resources to loyalist militias.

The case is now proceeding through the judicial system, with the religious figure scheduled for arraignment in the coming weeks. The prosecution’s action is being viewed as part of a broader effort to address extremist influence and to hold public figures accountable for their role in the conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Kazakhstan's newly formed pro-government party Adilet wins parliamentary election
content:
A newly formed political organization, Adilet, secured a decisive victory in the recent parliamentary elections, marking its first major electoral success since its establishment earlier this year. The party captured a substantial share of seats in the lower house, surpassing the thresholds required for representation and positioning itself as a dominant force within Kazakhstan’s legislative body.

Analysts note that Adilet’s win is likely to reinforce the authority of President Kassym‑Jomart Tokayev, whose administration has pursued a platform of political stability and economic reform. By aligning closely with the president’s agenda, the party is expected to support the implementation of his policy initiatives, thereby consolidating executive influence over the nation’s governance structure.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Netanyahu supports E1 settlement as elections approach
content:
Jerusalem – Israeli authorities’ recent approval of a new housing project in the West Bank has drawn criticism from Palestinian officials and international observers, who say the settlement undermines the prospect of a viable Palestinian state. The development, situated near a contested area slated for future negotiations, expands an existing bloc of Israeli homes and infrastructure, prompting the Palestinian leadership to label it a direct threat to the two‑state solution envisioned in past peace accords. The move comes amid heightened diplomatic pressure, with the United Nations and European Union urging restraint, while Israel’s own coalition government argues the construction is a lawful exercise of sovereignty over disputed territory.

The timing of the settlement’s endorsement is notable for domestic politics, as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other far‑right figures prepare for national elections later this year. Analysts suggest that the expansion may bolster the right‑wing bloc’s electoral appeal by signaling a firm stance on security and territorial claims, potentially swaying undecided voters who favor a hard‑line approach to the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict. As the election campaign intensifies, the settlement is likely to remain a focal point of debate, shaping both Israel’s internal political dynamics and its diplomatic relations with partners advocating for a negotiated pathway to Palestinian statehood.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Antonelli claims Mercedes lost F1 speed edge as Norris wins second straight race
content:
Lando Norris secured his second consecutive Formula 1 victory on Saturday, converting a pole‑position start into a win at the Dutch Grand Prix in Zandvoort. The McLaren driver led the field from the opening lap and maintained a commanding pace throughout the 72‑lap race, finishing ahead of his nearest rivals without significant challenge. Norris’s triumph follows his previous win at the British Grand Prix, marking the first back‑to‑back victories for the British driver since his debut season.

The victory lifts Norris to second place in the drivers’ championship, narrowing the gap to championship leader Max Verstappen, while McLaren gains valuable points in the constructors’ standings, moving closer to the top three. The team will look to build on the momentum heading into the upcoming summer events, with the next round scheduled for the Hungarian Grand Prix at the Hungaroring.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US threatens major economic sanctions on Iran, testing China ties
content:
Washington officials warned on Thursday that intensifying economic pressure on Tehran could trigger a retaliatory response from Beijing, complicating U.S. efforts to curb Iran’s nuclear and regional activities. The assessment, voiced by senior members of the State Department and Treasury, reflects concerns that tighter sanctions—particularly those targeting Iran’s oil exports and financial networks—might intersect with China’s growing commercial and strategic partnership with the Islamic Republic.

China, which accounts for roughly a third of Iran’s oil trade and has pledged to expand infrastructure projects under its Belt and Road Initiative, has previously signaled that it would defend its economic interests against unilateral measures it deems unjust. Analysts note that Beijing’s leverage in the United Nations Security Council and its capacity to provide alternative financing channels could blunt the impact of Western sanctions, prompting Washington to weigh the risk of a broader geopolitical backlash as it calibrates its policy toward Iran.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Norway's King Harald Hospitalized with Bloodstream Infection
content:
Oslo – Norway’s 86‑year‑old King Harald remains hospitalized as doctors treat him for a bloodstream bacterial infection. The monarch was admitted to the university hospital in early August after blood tests revealed the infection, and he is now receiving a course of intravenous antibiotics under close observation.

A spokesperson for the royal household confirmed that the king’s condition is stable and that he is responding to treatment, though no exact discharge date has been set. The palace noted that the king’s official duties will continue to be delegated to Crown Prince Haakon and other senior officials during his recovery. Medical staff expect a gradual improvement, and the royal family thanked the public for its concern while emphasizing that the king’s health remains the priority.
author: BBC World

title: Wildfire near Reno forces evacuation of nearly 90,000 residents
content:
A wildfire currently raging in the region has scorched approximately 10,500 acres, according to officials, and remains completely uncontained. The fire, which was first reported earlier this week, has prompted the activation of multiple fire‑management agencies and the deployment of ground crews and aerial resources in an effort to halt its spread.

Authorities continue to monitor the blaze closely, emphasizing that conditions such as dry vegetation and wind could influence its behavior. Evacuation orders and road closures have been issued for affected communities, and residents are advised to stay informed through official channels. The situation remains fluid, and officials will provide updates as containment efforts progress.
author: BBC World

title: DR Congo and M23 Agree on Peace Talks Roadmap, Switzerland Reports
content:
In a fragile cease‑fire that was brokered in Doha last year, the Democratic Republic of Congo’s government and the armed opposition signed an agreement aimed at ending hostilities in the eastern provinces. The accord was intended to halt the flow of violence that has plagued the region for decades, but the situation on the ground remains volatile.

Despite the formal truce, clashes continue to erupt across the mineral‑rich eastern DRC, where both sides vie for control over lucrative deposits of coltan, gold, and tin. The area’s long history of conflict—marked by inter‑ethnic tensions, militia activity, and external interference—has made it difficult for the agreement to take root. Sporadic skirmishes, ambushes, and artillery fire have persisted, undermining efforts to establish lasting peace and disrupting local communities.

The persistence of fighting underscores the challenges of translating diplomatic agreements into tangible security gains. While the Doha deal remains a legal framework for dialogue, the ongoing violence highlights the need for sustained international engagement and robust enforcement mechanisms to secure the region’s future stability.
author: Euronews

title: US Military Strikes Drug-Smuggling Boat in Pacific, Killing at Least Two
content:
The United States military announced the launch of Operation “Southern Spear” in early September, targeting drug trafficking networks that operate from Latin America. The operation, which is being carried out by U.S. Army and Marine Corps units in coordination with allied forces in the region, aims to disrupt the movement of narcotics into the United States and to dismantle the infrastructure that supports cartel operations.

President Donald Trump has characterized the conflict as a de facto war, stating that Washington is “effectively at war” with drug cartels that threaten national security and public safety. He cited rising drug‑related violence and the increasing sophistication of cartel logistics as key reasons for the military’s intervention. The administration has pledged additional resources, including intelligence sharing and joint training exercises, to strengthen the operation’s impact.

The operation’s launch follows years of escalating drug trafficking activity across the southern border. Analysts note that while the U.S. has long engaged in counter‑drug efforts, the formal military designation signals a heightened commitment to confronting the cartels. As the operation proceeds, officials will monitor its effectiveness in reducing drug flow and its broader implications for U.S. foreign policy in Latin America.
author: Euronews

title: Syria and Israel Hold US-Mediated Talks in Jordan to Defuse Tension
content:
Syria and Israel convened U.S.-mediated talks in Jordan on Sunday to de‑escalate a crisis triggered by an Israeli strike that Israel said was intended to prevent a Turkish military deployment in the region. The meeting, held at the Jordanian capital, brought together senior officials from both sides, with the United States acting as the primary facilitator.

The discussion focused on the immediate aftermath of the strike, the broader implications for regional security, and potential steps to prevent further escalation. Damascus emphasized its desire to remain uninvolved in the Israel‑Turkey dispute, while Israeli representatives reiterated their concern over Turkey’s military presence near the Golan Heights. U.S. diplomats highlighted the importance of maintaining open communication channels and urged both parties to adhere to agreed protocols to avoid a repeat of the incident.

The talks concluded with a mutual commitment to continue dialogue and to seek a peaceful resolution to the tensions. Officials on both sides expressed a willingness to engage in further negotiations, underscoring the role of the United States in fostering stability in the volatile region.
author: France 24

title: Canada suspends US trade talks after 50% tariffs imposed
content:
Ottawa announced on Tuesday that it is suspending ongoing trade negotiations with the United States after President Donald Trump unveiled a new round of tariffs that would impose a 50 percent duty on a broad range of Canadian imports. The tariffs, announced as part of the administration’s “America First” trade agenda, target sectors including steel, aluminum, dairy products, and certain agricultural goods, and are slated to take effect within the next 30 days. Canadian officials said the measures represent a sharp escalation in the trade dispute that began last year over softwood lumber and other issues, and they warned that the tariffs would significantly raise costs for Canadian exporters and consumers.

In response, the Canadian government pledged a “dollar‑for‑dollar” retaliation, indicating that equivalent tariffs would be applied to U.S. goods of comparable value. Trade Minister Mary Ng stated that Canada will work with industry partners to identify the specific products affected and will implement the countermeasures swiftly if the United States does not withdraw the proposed duties. The suspension of talks and the threat of reciprocal tariffs raise concerns about a broader trade war that could disrupt supply chains and dampen economic growth on both sides of the border, prompting analysts to call for diplomatic efforts to de‑escalate the conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gaza's healthcare system fails to reach displaced residents
content:
The Gaza Strip’s healthcare system, already strained by years of conflict, has collapsed to the point where it cannot reach the region’s most vulnerable residents—those living in displacement camps. Bombardments have destroyed hospitals, clinics, and supply chains, leaving medical personnel short of essential drugs, equipment, and power. In addition, the war’s infrastructure damage has cut off roads and bridges, preventing ambulances and aid convoys from entering densely populated camps such as Jabalia, Nuseirat, and al-Bureij.

Displaced families in these camps face a dire lack of medical care, with many children and pregnant women unable to obtain routine or emergency treatment. Humanitarian organizations report that the shortages of clean water, oxygen, and basic medical supplies have forced patients to travel long distances to the few functioning facilities, often under unsafe conditions. The cumulative effect is a growing number of untreated injuries, infections, and preventable deaths among the camp populations.

Urgent international intervention is required to restore essential health services and to ensure that displaced residents receive timely care. Without rapid repair of infrastructure and the delivery of medical supplies, the humanitarian crisis in Gaza’s displacement camps will continue to worsen, threatening the lives of thousands who are already in desperate need of assistance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: EU and Russian aircraft assist Serbia in fighting wildfires
content:
Serbian authorities are battling a series of large‑scale forest fires that have erupted across the country and neighboring Balkan states amid an unprecedented heatwave. By mid‑August, more than 1,200 hectares of woodland had been scorched in Serbia’s central and southern regions, prompting the government to request external assistance. The European Union’s Civil Protection Mechanism dispatched two rapid‑response teams equipped with fire‑fighting vehicles and water‑dropping helicopters, while Russia contributed a Beriev Be‑200 amphibious aircraft capable of delivering up to 3,000 litres of suppressant per sortie. Together, the multinational crews have conducted coordinated aerial and ground operations, focusing on protecting populated areas near the towns of Kraljevo and Niš and safeguarding critical infrastructure such as power lines and transport routes.

The extreme temperatures, which have consistently exceeded 40 °C, have intensified the spread of flames and hampered containment efforts throughout the Balkans, with parallel outbreaks reported in Bosnia‑Herzegovina, Montenegro and North Macedonia. Local fire services, supported by the EU and Russian assets, have reported a gradual reduction in the most active fire fronts, though hotspots remain in remote, densely forested zones. Officials say the combined international response underscores regional cooperation in the face of climate‑driven emergencies and will continue until the fires are fully extinguished and the affected areas are secured.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Petrol prices rise in over 145 countries after US‑Israel attacks on Iran
content:
At least 145 nations have reported rises in gasoline prices since the United States and Israel launched attacks on Iran, a development that underscores the broader market impact of heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. The assaults, which began in early June, have prompted concerns over the security of regional oil supplies and have triggered a reassessment of risk premiums by traders, leading to a noticeable uptick in crude‑oil futures and, consequently, retail fuel costs across diverse economies. Energy ministries and market analysts in Europe, Asia, Africa and the Americas have confirmed that the price increases are linked to both the immediate disruption of export routes and the anticipation of possible sanctions or further conflict that could constrain Iran’s output.

The widespread price hikes are expected to strain household budgets and could influence inflationary pressures in the affected countries, prompting some governments to consider temporary subsidies or tax adjustments to mitigate the impact. As the situation evolves, market observers note that continued instability in the region may sustain elevated fuel prices, while diplomatic efforts to de‑escalate the conflict could provide a pathway to stabilizing global energy markets.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trabzonspor president shocked by disallowed Salah goal
content:
Trabzonspor’s president, Ahmet Kaya, expressed disbelief after Mohamed Salah’s first start for the Turkish club ended with a disallowed goal in Saturday’s Süper Lig match against Antalyaspor. The Egyptian forward, who joined Trabzonspor in the summer transfer window, found the net in the 34th minute, only for the referee to overturn the decision following a VAR review.

The review determined that Salah had been offside in the buildup, prompting the officials to nullify the strike. Kaya, speaking to the press after the game, said the decision “was unexpected and contradictory to what we observed on the field,” and called for a clear explanation from the league’s disciplinary committee. Trabzonspor will continue their campaign with Salah available for upcoming fixtures, while the club awaits clarification on the VAR protocol applied in the incident.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gauff gears up for US Open with Cincinnati triumph
content:
Cincinnati, August 2026 – Coco Gauff captured the women’s singles title at the Cincinnati Open, defeating Jessica Pegula in the final to secure her first tournament victory of the 2026 season. The win comes just weeks before the U.S. Open, giving Gauff a strong momentum boost heading into the Grand Slam. Gauff’s triumph marks another milestone in her career, adding a prestigious hard‑court title to her growing résumé.

In the men’s draw, Frenchman Arthur Fils emerged victorious, claiming the championship in a hard‑court final that showcased his rising form on the WTA and ATP tours. Fils’ victory adds a significant title to his 2026 campaign and positions him as a contender for the upcoming majors. Both finalists’ performances underline the depth of talent present at the Cincinnati Open, a key lead‑up event for the U.S. Open.

The tournament’s outcomes set the stage for the U.S. Open, with Gauff and Fils entering the Grand Slam with confidence and recent success. Their victories at the Cincinnati Open highlight the importance of this event as a testing ground for players seeking to fine‑tune their game before the biggest tournament of the year.
author: BBC Sport

title: Labour Calls Reform's Social Housing Plan Unworkable
content:
Labour has blasted a new policy proposal from Reform, describing the plan as “unserious and unworkable” and accusing the party of pushing “gimmicks and division.” The criticism was issued in a statement released early this week, in which Labour leaders argued that the proposal fails to address key economic and social issues and instead relies on superficial measures that could exacerbate existing tensions.

Reform’s plan, unveiled in a recent policy briefing, was intended to overhaul several aspects of the current regulatory framework. Labour’s response highlights concerns that the reforms lack practical detail and may create further fragmentation within the political landscape. The party’s officials urged the government to adopt a more collaborative approach to policy development, citing the need for solutions that are both realistic and inclusive.

The exchange underscores the growing divide between the two parties as they prepare for the upcoming parliamentary session. While Reform continues to promote its agenda, Labour’s critique signals a readiness to challenge proposals that it views as insufficiently grounded, setting the stage for further debate on the direction of national policy.
author: BBC Politics

title: China says unmanned moon mission delayed over 'launch conditions'
content:
China’s manned space agency announced on Sunday that it will postpone the launch of the Chang’e‑7 lunar research mission, part of Beijing’s 2030 crewed lunar landing plan. The decision follows a rare launch failure on 24 June that damaged a Long March 5B rocket and its launch pad at the Wenchang Spacecraft Launch Site. The agency said the delay will allow for a thorough investigation of the failure and the necessary repairs before the next launch window.

Chang’e‑7 was originally slated for a mid‑2024 launch to study the Moon’s south pole and test new landing technologies. The postponement will shift its launch to the next available slot, likely in late 2024 or early 2025, according to CNSA officials. The agency emphasized that the delay does not alter China’s overall timeline for a crewed lunar landing, which remains targeted for 2030, and that the mission’s scientific objectives will still be achieved once the launch proceeds.

The setback underscores the technical challenges of lunar exploration but also highlights the robustness of China’s space program. By addressing the launch failure promptly, CNSA aims to maintain momentum on its lunar program and keep the 2030 crewed landing goal on track.
author: Phys.org

title: Thai PM meets security chiefs after coordinated attacks in three southern provinces
content:
A violent incident that took place early this morning in the city of Al‑Madinah has left at least 12 people injured and a number of buildings damaged.  Police and emergency services responded within minutes, treating the wounded and securing the area.  The attack, which involved a vehicle‑rampage and a small improvised explosive device, was carried out on a busy commercial street that had been crowded with shoppers and commuters.

As has often been the case with such incidents, no group was immediately publicly blamed or claimed responsibility for the actions.  Authorities have not yet identified a suspect or motive, and the investigation is underway.  The police are reviewing surveillance footage and interviewing witnesses, while the city’s mayor has called for calm and urged residents to stay vigilant.  The incident follows a series of similar attacks in the region over the past year, prompting a review of security protocols by the national counter‑terrorism unit.

The investigation remains ongoing, with officials promising to provide updates as more information becomes available.  Residents are advised to stay informed through official channels and to report any suspicious activity to local authorities.
author: Euronews

title: Gauff and Fils Capture Cincinnati Titles Ahead of US Open
content:
At the Cincinnati Open, world number one Coco Gauff secured her second title at the event by defeating top‑seeded Jessica Pegula in a decisive final. Gauff’s victory, achieved in straight sets, underscored her continued dominance on hard courts and added another hard‑court title to her growing résumé. The win also gave her a valuable boost in the rankings as the tournament’s points carry significant weight in the lead‑up to the US Open.

In a separate Masters 1000 final, Frenchman Alexandre Fils captured his first title of the year by overcoming compatriot and world number nine Jannik Tiafoe. Fils’ triumph came after a hard‑fought match that highlighted his resilience and tactical versatility, earning him a substantial leap in the ATP rankings. The victory marks a milestone for the young player, who has been steadily climbing the tour’s hierarchy.

Both finals highlighted the depth of talent in men’s and women’s tennis, with Gauff and Fils delivering compelling performances that will resonate throughout the remainder of the season. Their successes not only add to their individual accolades but also set the stage for heightened expectations in the upcoming Grand Slam events.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Salah nets two goals, sees two disallowed in Trabzonspor debut
content:
Mohamed Salah made his first appearance for the Turkish Super Lig side after signing on a free transfer earlier this month. The Egyptian international, who last played for Liverpool, was handed a starting berth in the club’s opening fixture of the season. The move was announced in early August, and Salah’s debut came in a home match against a mid‑table opponent.

The match, which finished 2‑1 in favour of Salah’s new team, saw the forward make an immediate impact. He opened the scoring with a well‑placed shot from the edge of the box and later provided an assist that sealed the win. Throughout the game, Salah displayed his trademark pace and link‑up play, drawing defenders and creating space for his teammates. His performance was praised by the coaching staff, who highlighted his ability to adapt quickly to the tactical demands of the Turkish league.

Salah’s successful debut underscores the club’s ambition to strengthen its attacking options and compete for domestic honours. With his experience and goal‑scoring pedigree, the team’s management expects him to be a key contributor over the course of the season. The transfer also signals the club’s willingness to recruit high‑profile talent on a free, potentially setting a precedent for future signings.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan army chief Munir visits Iran, offers channel between Tehran and Washington
content:
Islamabad announced on Tuesday that Pakistan is prepared to serve as an intermediary channel between Tehran and Washington, offering to convey messages and facilitate dialogue amid heightened tensions over Iran’s nuclear program and regional activities. The statement, made by a senior official in the foreign ministry, said the country’s “strategic location and longstanding ties with both capitals” position it to help de‑escalate the standoff and explore avenues for renewed diplomatic engagement. The offer comes as the United States has intensified sanctions on Iranian entities and Tehran has signaled openness to indirect talks, prompting regional powers to assess their roles in any potential back‑channel negotiations.

Analysts, however, remain divided on the extent of Pakistan’s leverage in such a delicate undertaking. Some observers note that Pakistan’s historic cooperation with both the United States and Iran, including trade links and security coordination, could grant it credibility as a conduit, while others point to limited recent diplomatic successes and the complex web of competing interests that may constrain its effectiveness. Past attempts by Islamabad to mediate in South Asian disputes have yielded mixed results, and the current geopolitical climate—marked by U.S. skepticism toward regional intermediaries and Tehran’s cautious approach to external mediation—adds further uncertainty. Nonetheless, officials say Pakistan will continue to explore its capacity to contribute to a constructive dialogue, acknowledging that any progress will depend on the willingness of both Washington and Tehran to engage through indirect channels.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ukraine hosts allies in Kyiv to discuss air‑defence amid drone attacks
content:
Leaders of the “Coalition of the Willing,” a group of Western nations that have pledged military assistance to Kyiv, convened on Thursday to address a growing shortfall in air‑defence equipment for Ukraine. The talks, held in Brussels, brought together senior officials from the United States, United Kingdom, Poland, the Baltic states and several other allies to assess supply chains, prioritize deliveries and explore additional funding mechanisms. Participants highlighted that recent Russian drone strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and the reciprocal use of unmanned aerial systems by Kyiv have intensified the demand for modern surface‑to‑air missiles and radar assets, which existing stockpiles are unable to fully meet.

In the interim, both sides have continued to employ drones as a primary tool of warfare, with Russia targeting power grids in the east and south, while Ukrainian forces have launched retaliatory attacks on logistical hubs in occupied territories. Coalition representatives affirmed their commitment to accelerate the provision of Patriot, NASAMS and other short‑range systems, and to coordinate with NATO’s air‑defence planning cell to streamline future transfers. The meeting concluded with an agreement to issue a joint statement outlining concrete delivery timelines and to reconvene in two weeks to review progress.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Maradona 1986 World Cup Hand of God ball sells for £2.5m at auction
content:
The football that Diego Maradona used to score the infamous “hand of God” goal during the 1986 World Cup quarter‑final against England is slated for auction. The ball, which also witnessed Maradona’s “Goal of the Century” in the same match, has been authenticated by FIFA and will be offered by a leading auction house later this month, with estimates placing its value in the six‑figure range.

The sale follows a series of high‑profile football memorabilia auctions that have drawn interest from collectors worldwide, reflecting the enduring historical significance of the 1986 tournament. Organizers expect strong bidding activity, citing the ball’s unique provenance and its status as a symbol of one of the sport’s most debated moments. The auction will provide an opportunity for a private collector to acquire a piece of World Cup history.
author: BBC World

title: Ceferin Criticizes Infantino's World Cup Stake Sale
content:
UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin criticised FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s proposal to sell a minority stake in the FIFA World Cup, describing the plan as “worse than the Super League.” Speaking at a UEFA gathering on Tuesday, Ceferin said the suggested sale of a 20 percent share to a consortium of private‑equity investors would jeopardise the competition’s integrity and commercial independence, echoing the backlash that the 2021 European Super League project generated among clubs, fans and regulators.
