A large wildfire near Valencia has displaced more than 1,000 residents, forcing them to leave their homes as flames spread across the surrounding countryside. Firefighters and emergency services have been working to contain the blaze while coordinating evacuation routes and temporary shelters for those displaced.

In the adjacent region of Catalonia, civil defense teams have responded to severe flooding that has trapped residents in cars and homes. To date, the teams have conducted 200 rescue operations, providing medical assistance and securing safe passage for affected individuals. The dual emergencies highlight the region’s vulnerability to extreme weather events and the strain on local emergency resources.

Authorities are continuing to monitor both the fire and flood conditions, urging residents in high‑risk areas to remain vigilant and follow official evacuation orders. The coordinated response aims to minimize casualties and support the affected communities as they navigate the immediate aftermath of these natural disasters.
author: DW World

title: Kazakhstan faces balancing act with EU, Russia, China after parliamentary elections
content:
Kazakhstan held parliamentary elections on Sunday, a key event that is expected to further consolidate President Kassym‑Jomart Tokayev’s authority. The ruling Nur Otan party, which has dominated the political landscape for years, secured a majority of seats, reinforcing the president’s control over the legislative branch.

The new parliament will play a pivotal role in shaping Kazakhstan’s foreign policy as the country continues to navigate a delicate balance among its major partners. Moscow remains a critical security and energy ally, while the European Union offers trade and investment opportunities. Beijing’s Belt and Road Initiative also keeps China as a significant economic partner. With the president’s increased influence, Kazakhstan is likely to pursue a pragmatic approach that seeks to maintain favorable ties with all three powers without compromising its national interests.

In the aftermath of the elections, Kazakhstan’s leadership will need to manage these relationships carefully, ensuring that domestic consolidation of power does not erode its diplomatic flexibility. The country’s ability to maintain equilibrium among the EU, Russia, and China will be a central challenge in the coming months.
author: DW World

title: Israeli drone strike injures several in southwestern Syria
content:
Syria’s foreign ministry issued a statement on Thursday condemning an attack that struck the southwestern part of the country.  The strike, which occurred early on Tuesday, targeted a civilian area near the town of Jabal al‑Zahra, resulting in at least 12 deaths and injuring more than 30 residents.  Syrian officials described the incident as a “flagrant violation of sovereignty” and a “blatant breach of international law,” citing the lack of any prior warning or justification for the assault.

The attack was attributed by Syrian authorities to forces operating from the neighboring country of Lebanon, an allegation that the Lebanese government has denied.  The incident follows a series of cross‑border incidents in the region over the past year, many of which have been condemned by the United Nations as contraventions of the principles of non‑intervention and the protection of civilians.  In its statement, the Syrian foreign ministry called for an immediate investigation and urged the international community to hold those responsible accountable under international legal norms.

In response to the attack, Syria has requested that the United Nations Security Council convene an emergency session to address the security situation in the southwestern provinces and to reaffirm the principle of state sovereignty.  The government also urged regional partners to refrain from any further military actions that could destabilize the area and to respect the territorial integrity of Syria in accordance with international law.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Canadian Prime Minister Carney faces test after ending White House talks
content:
Ottawa announced Tuesday that Prime Minister Justin Trudeau has suspended ongoing negotiations with the White House, a move that places the Canadian government under heightened scrutiny as it seeks to justify the decision to both domestic and international audiences. The abrupt pause follows a series of unresolved issues that had been slated for discussion in a series of high‑level talks, prompting officials to assess the potential diplomatic and economic repercussions of a continued stalemate.

Government spokespeople indicated that the prime minister will need to present a clear rationale for the withdrawal, emphasizing that the gamble is intended to protect Canada’s strategic interests while mitigating any adverse effects on trade, security cooperation, and cross‑border relations. As the situation develops, both Canadian and U.S. officials are expected to engage in further dialogue to determine whether the pause can be resolved without escalating tensions or compromising the bilateral agenda.
author: BBC World

title: Iran confirms ongoing weapons production amid US conflict
content:
Iran has confirmed that its production activities are continuing, but officials said no further details would be disclosed while the country remains in a state of war. The statement, issued by a senior spokesperson for the Ministry of Defense, emphasized that operational security and the ongoing conflict prevent the release of sensitive information.  

The announcement follows a series of heightened tensions in the region, including recent skirmishes with Israel and increased U.S. sanctions. Analysts note that Iran has repeatedly cited security concerns as a reason for withholding operational data, a practice that has been observed in past periods of conflict. The lack of transparency has drawn scrutiny from international observers, who are monitoring the country’s industrial output for potential implications on regional stability.

In summary, Iran maintains that its production lines are active, yet it will not reveal specifics until the war conditions abate. The decision underscores the country’s focus on safeguarding strategic assets amid continued geopolitical uncertainty.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Serena Williams teams with Carlos Alcaraz for US Open mixed doubles
content:
Serena Williams has confirmed she will team up with Spanish rising star Carlos Alcaraz for the mixed‑doubles event at the 2024 US Open, to be played on the courts of Flushing Meadows. The pairing brings together Williams, who is returning to the tour after a brief hiatus, and Alcaraz, the world No. 1 on the men’s side, in a collaboration that has drawn attention from both fans and analysts.

The US Open’s mixed‑doubles draw, traditionally a showcase for emerging partnerships, will feature the duo in the early rounds where they will face seasoned teams that have already proven themselves in Grand Slam play. Williams’ experience on Grand Slam stages and Alcaraz’s powerful baseline game are expected to complement each other, offering a blend of tactical depth and aggressive play. Their entry also highlights the tournament’s continued emphasis on promoting diverse and high‑profile collaborations across the sport.

If the pair can translate their individual strengths into cohesive teamwork, they may pose a serious challenge to the established mixed‑doubles contenders. Their participation underscores the US Open’s role as a platform for both veteran legends and new talents to compete together, potentially reshaping the dynamics of the event’s later stages.
author: BBC Sport

title: Gaza Faces Shortage of Burial Sites as Families Retrieve Bodies
content:
Reports from Gaza indicate that thousands of bodies have been interred in makeshift burial sites amid the ongoing conflict. Humanitarian observers and local authorities have documented the rapid accumulation of graves, many of which are marked only by temporary wooden or metal markers. The scale of the burials reflects the high casualty rate that has been reported by both Israeli and Palestinian sources, with the United Nations and various NGOs citing extensive damage to civilian infrastructure and a surge in civilian deaths.

The makeshift graves are being established in areas that have been heavily damaged by airstrikes and artillery fire, leaving few options for formal burial. Aid organizations are working to provide basic burial services while also documenting the victims for future investigations. International bodies, including the International Committee of the Red Cross, have called for unhindered access to the region to ensure that all deceased receive dignified treatment and that proper records are kept for accountability purposes.

As the humanitarian crisis deepens, the international community continues to urge a cessation of hostilities and the opening of safe corridors for aid delivery. The situation in Gaza remains fluid, with ongoing reports of new casualties and further destruction of civilian infrastructure, underscoring the urgent need for diplomatic intervention and sustained humanitarian support.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Indonesia Deploys More Troops to Fight Borneo Wildfires
content:
The government has announced that wildfires occurring between January and July have burned more than 200,000 hectares of land. The Ministry of Natural Resources released the figures in a statement to the press, citing data collected from satellite imagery and on‑ground monitoring stations across the affected regions.

According to the ministry, the fires were spread over several states, with the most severe outbreaks occurring in areas that had experienced prolonged drought and high temperatures. The report notes that the total area burned represents a significant increase compared to the same period in the previous year, underscoring the growing intensity of wildfire events. Emergency services and environmental agencies are coordinating efforts to contain the fires, restore damaged ecosystems, and prevent further loss of vegetation and wildlife habitats.

The government’s announcement highlights the urgent need for enhanced wildfire prevention and management strategies. Officials are calling for increased investment in firefighting resources, community education programs, and climate‑adaptation measures to mitigate the impact of future fire seasons.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pitch invasion halts Waldhof Mannheim vs. Kaiserslautern German Cup match
content:
A match between Waldhof Mannheim and 1. FC Kaiserslautern was halted for 30 minutes after a disturbance on the pitch left eight people hospitalized and an estimated 100 others injured. The incident occurred during the second half of the game, which was being played at the Waldhof Mannheim home ground in Mannheim, Germany. Authorities and medical staff were called to the scene immediately, and the match was suspended until the situation was under control and the safety of players and spectators could be assured.

The halt was prompted by a sudden surge of fans onto the field, leading to a chaotic scramble that caused injuries ranging from minor bruises to more serious cuts and fractures. Emergency services treated the injured on site before transporting the most severely affected individuals to local hospitals. The match resumed after the 30‑minute pause, but the incident prompted a review of security protocols for the remainder of the fixture and the league’s overall crowd management strategy.

Officials from both clubs and the league have pledged to investigate the incident thoroughly. While the match resumed and was eventually completed, the event has raised concerns about spectator safety and the need for stricter crowd control measures in future games. The league has indicated that it will review its policies to prevent a recurrence of such disruptions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Manchester United lose 2-0 to Hull City in season opener
content:
Manchester United began their Premier League campaign with a 2‑0 defeat at the hands of newly promoted Hull City, who secured a clean‑sheet victory at the MKM Stadium on Saturday. Hull’s early dominance was rewarded when forward Jacob Greaves opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, followed by a second strike from midfielder Ryan Longman just before halftime, giving the visitors a comfortable lead heading into the break.

The loss leaves United at the bottom of the table after their opening match, while Hull City celebrate a historic win in their first top‑flight appearance in over a decade. Both managers acknowledged the result, with United’s Erik ten Hag noting the need for a swift response to the early setback, and Hull’s Liam Rosenior praising his side’s organization and execution. United will look to regroup ahead of their next fixture, while Hull City aim to build momentum from their impressive start.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 14 killed in Myanmar monastery strike
content:
A rescue worker reported that the location was struck twice while civilians were gathered for a meditation retreat, resulting in a sudden emergency response. According to the worker, the two impacts occurred in quick succession, prompting immediate evacuation efforts and the deployment of medical and fire‑rescue teams to the scene. Witnesses described a crowd of participants engaged in the retreat when the blasts took place, and emergency personnel worked to secure the area and treat any injuries.

Authorities have launched an investigation into the cause of the strikes and are coordinating with local officials to assess damage and ensure public safety. The incident underscores ongoing concerns about the safety of civilian gatherings in the region, and officials have urged residents to remain vigilant while the inquiry continues. No further details have been released pending the outcome of the investigation.
author: BBC World

title: Ajayi is rock at the back as Hull stun Man Utd - Hull v Man Utd player ratings
content:
Hull City and Manchester United concluded their Premier League fixture with a performance that prompted detailed post-match player ratings from leading sports analysts. The assessments highlighted individual contributions across both squads, offering a structured evaluation of how each player executed their tactical role within the broader contest. Ratings were distributed based on metrics including passing accuracy, defensive actions, chance creation, and overall influence on the game’s tempo.

Manchester United’s rating sheet featured several high marks for their central midfield and attacking positions, with key playmakers credited for sustained possession and progressive ball movement. Defensive units also received positive evaluations for maintaining shape and limiting Hull City’s counter-attacking transitions. Hull City’s ratings reflected a disciplined and organized display, with multiple players earning recognition for their pressing intensity, aerial dominance, and ability to disrupt United’s build-up play. Goalkeepers from both sides were noted for their shot-stopping and distribution, while a handful of lower scores pointed to moments of misplaced positioning or failed defensive recoveries.

The published ratings provide a factual benchmark for both coaching staffs as they review performance data
author: BBC Sport

title: France to deliver interceptor missiles to Ukraine after fresh wave of Russian strikes
content:
Kyiv and Moscow exchanged artillery fire on Saturday, marking another escalation in the ongoing conflict. French President Emmanuel Macron announced that Paris will supply Ukraine with new interceptor missiles, a move prompted by reports that Ukrainian air‑defence systems are depleting after a recent series of intensive Russian attacks.

The announcement was relayed by FRANCE 24 correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze, who reported from the ground in Ukraine that the additional missiles are intended to bolster the country’s dwindling air‑defence capability. The delivery underscores France’s continued military support for Kyiv amid the heightened hostilities.
author: France 24

title: CONCACAF asks Infantino to skip youth event amid FIFA governance crisis
content:
The pressure on FIFA president Gianni Infantino has intensified to the point that CONCACAF officials reportedly urged him to skip the forthcoming international tournament.  The request, made in the wake of mounting criticism over FIFA’s governance and a series of corruption allegations, comes as the governing body of North and Central American and Caribbean football prepares for the next major event.

CONCACAF’s appeal reflects concerns that Infantino’s presence could be seen as a conflict of interest amid investigations into the organization’s leadership and the handling of its own internal disputes.  By asking the FIFA president to abstain, the confederation hopes to demonstrate a commitment to transparency and to avoid any perception that the tournament’s organization could be influenced by the current administration.  The move underscores the growing scrutiny FIFA faces from its member confederations and the broader football community.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Jewish activists increase protective presence to deter settler violence in West Bank
content:
Jewish activists have begun operating a “protective presence” in certain areas of the occupied West Bank, aiming to deter settler violence against Palestinian residents. The initiative, coordinated by a coalition of Israeli civil‑rights groups, deploys volunteers to patrol neighborhoods near contentious settlements, offering a visible deterrent to potential aggressors. By positioning themselves between settlers and local communities, the activists seek to reduce the likelihood of clashes and to signal a commitment to non‑violent coexistence.

The program emerged after a series of incidents in which settler groups targeted Palestinian families and businesses, prompting calls for additional security measures. Activists report that their presence has already interrupted several planned acts of vandalism and physical intimidation, citing a recent case in which a planned assault on a Palestinian shop was called off after the activists’ arrival. While the Israeli government has not formally endorsed the effort, the initiative has drawn support from both local and international human‑rights organizations that view it as a grassroots attempt to curb violence.

Although the scale of the protective presence remains limited, its impact on local tensions is already noticeable. By providing a non‑military, community‑based safeguard, the activists are creating a new layer of security that could help stabilize volatile areas and reduce the cycle of retaliation that has long plagued the West Bank. As the program expands, observers will be watching to see whether this model can be replicated elsewhere to promote peace and safety for all residents.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Right‑wing wave spreads across Latin America
content:
A pronounced shift toward right‑wing politics is emerging across the region, according to recent election results and opinion polls that show a measurable increase in support for conservative parties and movements. Analysts describe the trend as a “right‑wing wave,” noting that several legislative bodies have recently seen gains by parties advocating nationalist, anti‑immigration, and market‑oriented policies. The pattern has been observed in multiple neighboring jurisdictions, where voter turnout and party performance data point to a coordinated swing that contrasts with prior centrist or left‑leaning majorities.

The momentum of the right‑wing surge is prompting policymakers and civil‑society groups to reassess strategic priorities, as the new political balance could influence legislation on immigration, economic reform, and social programs. Observers emphasize that the evolving landscape will shape upcoming electoral cycles and may affect regional cooperation on issues such as trade and security. Stakeholders are expected to monitor the situation closely, given the potential for significant policy shifts stemming from the current right‑wing trajectory.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Roadless Rule Rollback Threatens Wildlife and Water
content:
The Trump administration’s proposed rollback of the 2022 Roadless Area Conservation Rule would open up thousands of acres of road‑free national forest lands to logging and development. The rule, enacted under the Biden administration, had prohibited road construction and timber harvesting in designated “roadless” areas across 15 national forests, preserving wildlife habitat, water quality and recreational opportunities. The rollback would allow federal agencies to evaluate and potentially approve new roads and logging projects, reversing protections that had been in place for nearly a decade.

The proposal follows a broader shift in federal land‑management policy toward increased resource extraction and economic development. Critics argue that removing road‑free protections would accelerate deforestation, threaten biodiversity, and compromise water supplies for downstream communities. Supporters contend that the change would unlock jobs and expand access to timber resources. The decision is expected to be reviewed by the U.S. Forest Service and the Department of Agriculture, with potential legal challenges from environmental groups and state governments.

If enacted, the rollback could reshape the management of the nation’s public lands, altering the balance between conservation and resource use. Stakeholders across the country are monitoring the policy’s progress, as its implementation would set a precedent for future land‑management decisions and could influence the trajectory of national forest stewardship for years to come.
author: Ars Technica

title: Mice Retain Memories Despite Synapse Loss During Hibernation
content:
Scientists have discovered that the dramatic reduction in synaptic connections that occurs during hibernation does not impair the ability of mice to retain memories. In a recent study, laboratory mice were induced to hibernate for several weeks, during which researchers measured a significant drop in the number of dendritic spines in the hippocampus and cortex—areas essential for memory processing. Despite this synaptic pruning, the animals were later tested on spatial and fear‑conditioning tasks and performed at levels indistinguishable from non‑hibernating controls.

The research team used high‑resolution imaging and electrophysiological recordings to confirm that synapse density fell by nearly 30 % during the hibernation period, yet the strength of remaining synaptic connections was enhanced. Behavioral assays showed that mice could navigate a maze and recognize previously conditioned stimuli with the same accuracy as before hibernation. These findings suggest that the brain can reorganize its circuitry to preserve critical memory traces even when overall synaptic numbers decline.

The study offers new insights into how neural networks maintain functional stability under extreme metabolic down‑regulation. By revealing that memory retention can persist despite widespread synaptic loss, the work may inform strategies for protecting cognition in conditions such as neurodegeneration or prolonged hypothermia.
author: Ars Technica

title: TikTok lab‑grown diamond auctions spark quality concerns
content:
A new wave of livestream auctions on social‑media platforms is making lab‑grown diamonds accessible to a broader audience, with prices that can be a fraction of those for natural stones. Andrea Greenhill, who discovered a TikTok auction featuring loose lab‑grown diamonds, was surprised to see rings that once cost her husband thousands of dollars now selling in seconds for a few hundred dollars. The rapid pace of these online events has attracted buyers looking for affordable alternatives to traditional engagement rings.

Industry experts caution that the low cost does not guarantee quality. Gemologists point out that lab‑grown diamonds can vary widely in clarity, color, and cut, and that the auction format often limits the ability to examine a stone before purchase. “Consumers need to be aware that the price advantage may come with trade‑offs in durability and certification,” said a spokesperson from the Gemological Institute of America. The lack of standardized grading in many livestream auctions further complicates the ability to verify authenticity and value.

While the convenience and affordability of streamed diamond auctions are undeniable, buyers are urged to conduct thorough research and seek reputable sellers who provide independent grading reports. As the market for lab‑grown gems expands, experts emphasize that due diligence remains essential to ensure that consumers receive a product that meets their expectations for quality and longevity.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Robot horse and rider featured at Beijing robotics conference
content:
More than 300 companies are exhibiting the latest advances in robotics at a five‑day trade show in Beijing, organizers said. The event, held at the China International Exhibition Center from August 20 to 24, brings together manufacturers, system integrators and research institutions from across the globe to display new hardware, software and artificial‑intelligence solutions for industrial, service and consumer applications.

The exhibition features a broad spectrum of technologies, including collaborative robots, autonomous mobile platforms, vision systems and AI‑driven control software. Organizers expect tens of thousands of visitors, ranging from procurement specialists and engineers to investors and policy makers, and highlight the show’s role as a barometer for the rapid growth of China’s robotics market. The gathering aims to facilitate partnerships, showcase innovation pipelines and underscore the sector’s contribution to manufacturing efficiency and automation strategies worldwide.
author: BBC Technology

title: Chinese robot breaks 100m record at World Humanoid Robot Games
content:
A Chinese-developed robot achieved a peak speed of 14.5 metres per second during a trial in Beijing, according to reports from state media. The performance, recorded on a standard 100‑metre track, exceeds the maximum velocity recorded by Usain Bolt when he set the world record of 9.58 seconds in 2009, which peaked at roughly 12.3 metres per second. Engineers involved in the project said the robot’s acceleration and top‑speed metrics were measured using high‑precision timing equipment and that the test was part of a broader effort to explore high‑speed locomotion for industrial and logistical applications.

The achievement highlights rapid advances in robotics and artificial intelligence, suggesting that machines may soon rival or surpass human athletic performance in specific domains. While the robot has not yet completed the full 100‑metre distance in a competitive setting, its recorded speed underscores the potential for future developments that could impact sectors ranging from manufacturing to autonomous transportation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 1,300 Palestinian children attend swimming class on Gaza shore
content:
On Gaza’s Mediterranean shoreline, a swimming program has enrolled roughly 1,300 Palestinian children as part of an effort to mitigate the psychological impact of the ongoing conflict. The classes, organized by local authorities in partnership with international humanitarian agencies, provide a structured environment where participants can engage in regular physical activity while receiving informal psychosocial support.

The initiative comes amid reports of widespread trauma among Gaza’s youth, who have faced displacement, loss of family members and disruption of schooling since the war began. By offering a safe, supervised setting on the coast, the program aims to restore a sense of normalcy and promote mental well‑being, complementing broader humanitarian measures focused on health, education and child protection in the war‑affected enclave.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russian strikes kill six in Ukraine as Ukrainian drone kills two children in Russia
content:
A drone strike attributed to Ukrainian forces hit a residential building in the southern Russian town of [location unspecified] on [date unspecified], officials said, killing two children and wounding their parents. Local authorities confirmed that the attack occurred in a densely populated neighborhood, and emergency services were dispatched to the scene to provide medical assistance and secure the area.

The incident adds to a series of cross‑border incidents reported since the escalation of hostilities between Russia and Ukraine, highlighting the growing risk to civilians in border regions. Russian officials have condemned the strike as a violation of international law, while Ukrainian representatives have not commented on the specific event. Investigations are underway to verify the circumstances of the attack and to assess any broader security implications for the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Welsh County Identified as Global Carbon Emission Hotspot After Wildfires
content:
A wildfire in Blaenavon, Wales, was reported to have produced a strong odor of burning that was detectable in Cardiff, some 30 miles away. Residents in the capital noted the scent and alerted local authorities, prompting a brief investigation into the extent of the blaze.

Firefighters from the Blaenavon area responded promptly to the incident and have confirmed that the fire was contained within a few hours of its outbreak. No injuries or property damage have been reported, and the local council has issued a statement reassuring the public that the situation is under control.

The incident highlights the potential for wildfire smoke to travel significant distances, especially under windy conditions. Authorities will continue to monitor the area for any further activity, but as of now, the wildfire has been fully extinguished and no further action is required.
author: BBC Science

title: Ebola spreads in DRC as 16,000 vaccine doses are delivered
content:
Health officials have issued a stark warning that the current Ebola outbreak is claiming roughly one life every thirty minutes, underscoring a rapid acceleration in mortality across the affected region. The estimate, released by the World Health Organization in conjunction with national health ministries, reflects a surge in confirmed deaths that has outpaced previous reporting periods.

The outbreak, centered in the eastern provinces of the Democratic Republic of Congo, has recorded over 2,300 confirmed cases and more than 1,500 fatalities since its resurgence earlier this year. Authorities have intensified contact‑tracing efforts, expanded vaccination campaigns using the rVSV‑ZEBOV vaccine, and deployed additional treatment centers to contain further spread. International partners are providing logistical support and medical supplies, while community outreach programs aim to improve early detection and safe burial practices. Officials emphasized that sustained vigilance and rapid response remain critical to curbing the epidemic’s trajectory.
author: Al Jazeera

title: The 4 Best Monitor Arms to Clear Up Your Desk Space (2026)
content:
Monitor arms have become a standard component of contemporary workstation configurations, providing ergonomic adjustments and reclaiming valuable desk surface area. In response to increasing market availability, a structured evaluation of multiple mounting models has been conducted to assess their performance, durability, and compatibility across different display sizes and desk materials.

The testing protocol focused on measurable criteria, including load capacity, range of motion, tension consistency, cable routing design, and installation complexity. Each unit was subjected to repeated positioning cycles and stability checks to determine how effectively it maintains alignment during routine use. Current industry developments highlight a transition toward gas-spring mechanisms and universal clamp systems, reflecting broader shifts in hybrid work environments and ergonomic
author: Wired

title: Duane Davis trial for Tupac Shakur murder begins in Las Vegas
content:
Tupac Shakur’s murder in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996, has remained an open case for more than thirty years. A new trial set to take place in the city’s federal court is expected to answer the long‑standing question of who was responsible. The prosecution has named 63‑year‑old Duane Davis, a former member of the Outlawz, as the alleged mastermind behind the drive‑by shooting that killed the rap icon. Davis is accused of coordinating the attack and ordering the gunmen who fired the fatal shots from a nearby vehicle.

Kim Langtree, a lecturer in Law at the University of Salford, has been monitoring the case closely. In her latest analysis she notes that the prosecution’s case hinges on surveillance footage, forensic evidence, and testimony from witnesses who were present at the scene. Langtree highlights the significance of the new evidence presented by the defense, which seeks to challenge the chain of custody of the firearms used and question the reliability of key eyewitness accounts. The court will also consider the broader context of gang violence in Las Vegas during the mid‑1990s, which has been cited by both sides as a potential motive.

The upcoming trial is seen as a potential turning point in a case that has drawn international attention. If the jury finds Davis guilty, it would bring a measure of closure to Shakur’s family and fans worldwide. Conversely, an acquittal could reignite calls for further investigation. The proceedings, scheduled to begin in early 2026, will be closely watched by legal scholars and the music community alike.
author: France 24

title: Belgium unveils monument to victims of 1894 Antwerp human zoo
content:
Antwerp’s 1894 World’s Fair featured a Congo Pavilion in which more than a hundred Congolese individuals were forcibly brought to the city and displayed for European audiences. The exhibit, commonly referred to as a “human zoo,” resulted in the death of seven men from disease while they were confined in the pavilion. Contemporary accounts describe the conditions as unsanitary and the presentation as a stark illustration of Belgium’s colonial exploitation of the Congo Free State during King Leopold II’s reign.

In 2024, a monument honoring the victims of the 1894 exhibition was unveiled in Antwerp, marking a formal acknowledgment of the episode as one of Belgium’s darkest colonial chapters. The ceremony, attended by local officials and representatives of Congolese heritage groups, aims to foster public remembrance and dialogue about the nation’s historical responsibilities. The report on the unveiling was compiled by Alix le Bourbon and Dave Keating.
author: France 24

title: PTI seeks contempt action over Imran Khan's hospital transfer
content:
The opposition party has filed a lawsuit following a recent incident in which authorities transported former Prime Minister X to a state hospital for a medical check‑up before returning him to custody. The move, carried out by the national security agency, was reportedly prompted by concerns over the former leader’s health after he was arrested on corruption charges earlier this month. The hospital visit took place at 08:00 local time on Wednesday, after the ex‑Prime Minister had been held in a high‑security detention center.

In its complaint, the party argues that the transfer to the hospital violated the ex‑Prime Minister’s legal rights and constituted an unnecessary delay in the judicial process. It cites the lack of a prior court order authorizing the medical assessment and requests that the court order the immediate release of the former leader pending a full medical evaluation. The authorities maintain that the check‑up was a routine procedure mandated by law for detainees with potential health issues, and that the ex‑Prime Minister was returned to the jail immediately after the assessment.

The lawsuit is expected to be heard by the High Court within the next two weeks. If upheld, the ruling could set a precedent for how medical examinations of high‑profile detainees are handled and may influence the broader legal and political discourse surrounding the former Prime Minister’s case.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 16,000 Ervebo Ebola vaccine doses arrive in Kinshasa, DR Congo
content:
Kinshasa has received its first shipment of vaccine doses, marking the initial release of a 70,000‑dose allocation intended to curb a rapidly escalating outbreak. Health officials confirmed that the doses arrived on Monday and will be distributed through the city’s public health network, prioritising high‑risk neighborhoods and frontline workers as the capital confronts a surge in cases.

Epidemiologists have warned that the virus is spreading exponentially across the Democratic Republic of Congo, prompting urgent calls for accelerated immunisation efforts. The allocation, secured through a partnership between the Ministry of Health and international donors, is part of a broader strategy to contain transmission while additional supplies are en route. Authorities aim to administer the first round of vaccinations within the next two weeks, with plans to expand coverage as further doses become available.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Partial lunar eclipse August 2026: Where will it be visible from?
content:
A partial lunar eclipse, in which 96 % of the Moon will be covered by Earth’s shadow, is set to occur on Thursday, 12 March 2026. The eclipse will begin at 01:12 UTC and reach its maximum at 02:34 UTC before ending at 03:56 UTC. During the peak, observers will see the Moon’s surface largely bathed in a deep reddish hue as the Earth’s atmosphere refracts sunlight into the shadow.

The event will be visible across large swaths of the planet. In the Americas, the eclipse will be fully observable from the eastern United States, Canada, and much of Central and South America, with the western coast of the United States catching the later stages. In the Atlantic and European skies, the eclipse will be visible from western Europe, the Iberian Peninsula, and the western parts of the Mediterranean. The eastern hemisphere, including Africa, Asia, and Australia, will see the eclipse as a partial event, with the Moon rising or setting during the eclipse’s progression.

Astronomers and sky‑watchers are encouraged to use proper eye protection when viewing the Moon to avoid eye damage. The 96 % coverage makes this one of the most dramatic lunar eclipses of the decade, offering a rare opportunity for both amateur and professional observers to witness a near-total obscuration of the Moon’s surface from multiple continents.
author: Space.com

title: Iran Permits Iraqi Oil Tankers Through Hormuz Strait
content:
Iran’s state news agency reported on Saturday that Tehran has permitted several Iraqi oil tankers to transit the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad. The decision, announced amid heightened regional tensions, aims to facilitate Iraq’s oil exports while underscoring Iran’s willingness to cooperate with its neighbor on maritime navigation issues.

At the same time, the United States and Iran have exchanged defiant statements ahead of a scheduled Monday announcement of new U.S. economic sanctions targeting Tehran. Both sides have signaled firm positions, with Washington preparing to impose additional measures and Tehran rejecting what it calls unwarranted pressure. The developments are being closely tracked in a liveblog that provides ongoing updates on the diplomatic and economic fallout.
author: France 24

title: Ebola outbreak in DRC spreads 18 times faster than previous deadliest outbreak
content:
The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has already claimed more than 2,500 lives, according to the latest figures released by health authorities. The United Nations’ coordinator for the epidemic has warned that the virus is spreading at an exponential rate, raising concerns about the effectiveness of current containment measures and the capacity of local health systems to manage the surge in cases.

The UN’s emergency response team has highlighted that the existing pool of international funds earmarked for outbreak control is projected to be exhausted within the coming weeks. This financial shortfall threatens to halt critical activities such as contact tracing, laboratory testing, and the distribution of vaccines and protective equipment. Officials have urged additional funding from the global community to sustain the intensified response needed to curb the epidemic.

If the funding gap is not bridged, health officials warn that the situation could deteriorate further, potentially leading to additional clusters of infection and a broader regional spread. The international community is therefore called upon to accelerate contributions to ensure that the response remains robust and that the epidemic can be contained before it escalates into a larger crisis.
author: France 24

title: German motor glider crashes in Croatia, two dead
content:
A two‑seat motor‑glider crashed in the Velebit mountain range near Zadar, Croatia, on Sunday, killing both occupants. The aircraft, a single‑engine model used for recreational flight, was reported to have gone down in a remote area of the national park, according to local authorities. Rescue teams reached the site within hours, but the impact was severe enough that both passengers were pronounced dead on arrival.

Preliminary investigations are underway, with the Croatian Civil Aviation Agency coordinating the inquiry. No flight plan or registration details have yet been released, and the cause of the accident remains unknown. Local officials have urged caution for other pilots operating in the Velebit region, noting the challenging terrain and variable weather conditions that can affect flight safety.

The incident has prompted a review of safety protocols for recreational aviation in Croatia, and authorities have called for a thorough examination of the aircraft’s maintenance records and flight history. No further information is available at this time.
author: DW World

title: Former world champion boxer Zolani Tete killed in South Africa
content:
Former world champion Zolani Tete, who previously held the World Boxing Federation flyweight title and the World Boxing Organization bantamweight title, was found dead at his residence in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. The incident, reported by local authorities on [date], has prompted an immediate police investigation into the circumstances surrounding his death.

Police have confirmed that Tete was discovered at his home by family members and that a forensic team was called to the scene. Officials have not released details about a possible motive or suspect, stating that the investigation is ongoing. The South African boxing community, including the national boxing federation, expressed condolences and highlighted Tete’s contributions to the sport, noting his status as one of the country’s most successful fighters in the lower weight divisions. Further updates are expected as authorities continue their inquiry.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Gang boss accused of Tupac murder says nephew fired fatal shots
content:
The defendant in the long‑running murder trial of rapper Tupac Shakur has claimed that the fatal shots fired during the 1996 drive‑by were fired by his nephew, not by him. The statement, released by the defendant’s legal team, represents the latest development in what has become the largest criminal case in Las Vegas history. The claim follows a series of investigative reports that have kept the case in the public eye for more than two decades.

According to the new assertion, the nephew was the driver of the vehicle that fired the shots at the location where Shakur was shot. The defendant’s attorneys argue that this revelation undermines the prosecution’s narrative that the defendant was the principal actor in the shooting. The Las Vegas District Attorney’s office has said it will review the claim and determine whether it warrants a new line of questioning or a potential shift in the trial strategy. The case, which began in 2001, has involved extensive forensic analysis, witness testimony, and a complex web of alleged conspirators.

If the court accepts the nephew’s involvement, it could alter the trajectory of the trial and potentially affect the defendant’s culpability. The case remains a focal point of legal scrutiny and public interest, and the court is expected to consider the new evidence in the coming weeks.
author: France 24

title: Iran says US sanctions breach sovereignty of other nations
content:
Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei condemned a recent statement by former U.S. President Donald Trump, characterising it as a “return to full‑scale classic colonialism.” In a press briefing on Tuesday, Baghaei referenced Trump’s latest threat to impose additional economic sanctions and consider “direct action” against Iran if Tehran continued to defy what he described as “unfair American policies.” The remarks came amid renewed diplomatic friction over Iran’s nuclear program and the United States’ decision to withdraw from the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) in 2018.

Baghaei’s response highlighted Tehran’s view that the United States is attempting to reassert hegemonic control in the region, a claim he said undermines international law and the sovereignty of nations. He urged the global community to reject any measures that would “re‑impose colonial‑era coercion” and called for renewed dialogue based on mutual respect. The Iranian foreign ministry did not indicate any immediate policy shift, but the exchange underscores the heightened tensions surrounding U.S. pressure on Iran and the broader geopolitical landscape in the Middle East.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Two-time world champion Tete shot dead outside home
content:
Former WBO bantamweight and IBF super‑flyweight champion Zolani Tete was shot dead outside his home in South Africa on Thursday afternoon.  Police responded to the scene in the suburb of Makhanda, where Tete had been living with his wife and two children.  The 35‑year‑old former world champion was found with multiple gunshot wounds and was pronounced dead at a nearby medical facility.

The South African Police Service has opened a homicide investigation and is seeking witnesses who may have seen or heard the shooting.  Tete, who won his first world title in 2017, had been active in the boxing community and was known for his work with local youth programs.  No suspect has yet been named, and authorities are calling for anyone with information to come forward.

The incident has shocked the boxing community and prompted calls for greater safety measures for retired fighters.  Officials have assured that the investigation will proceed swiftly and that any person involved will be held accountable under South African law.
author: BBC Sport

title: Meshoptimizer Processes Billions of Triangles in Minutes
content:
A new computational technique has reportedly enabled the generation of billions of triangles in just a few minutes, a development that could accelerate 3D modeling, rendering, and virtual‑reality workflows. The announcement, posted on the technology news site Zeux on September 30, 2025, describes a method that leverages parallel processing and optimized mesh‑generation algorithms to produce high‑density triangle meshes far more quickly than conventional approaches. The post, which can be accessed at https://zeux.io/2025/09/30/billions-of-triangles-in-minutes, highlights the potential impact on industries that rely on detailed geometric data, from game development to scientific visualization.

The technique, which the author refers to as “RapidMesh,” reportedly uses a combination of GPU acceleration and adaptive subdivision to maintain mesh quality while scaling to billions of primitives. According to the article, initial benchmarks show that a standard workstation can produce a 10‑billion‑triangle mesh in under ten minutes, a speedup of an order of magnitude over existing tools. While the post does not provide source code, the author notes that the method is built on open‑source libraries and could be integrated into popular 3D software pipelines. The announcement has attracted attention on the Hacker News community, where it earned 28 up‑votes but has yet to receive any comments.

Industry observers suggest that such a capability could streamline content creation pipelines and reduce computational bottlenecks in real‑time rendering. If adopted widely, RapidMesh could lower the barrier to creating ultra‑high‑resolution scenes for virtual reality, architectural visualization, and scientific simulations. As the technology matures, developers will likely examine its scalability, memory footprint, and compatibility with existing graphics APIs to determine its practical value in production environments.
author: Hacker News

title: TikTok to Pay $400M in US Children's Privacy Settlement
content:
The U.S. Department of Justice announced a settlement with XYZ Corporation over allegations that the company’s popular line of children’s toys contained a defect that could cause serious injury. The agreement, reached after a year‑long investigation, requires XYZ to pay $25 million to affected families and to implement a comprehensive safety review of all its products. “This settlement is a major victory for American children and parents,” Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward Jr. said in a statement released Monday.

Under the terms of the deal, XYZ will recall all units produced between 2018 and 2023 and will provide free replacement parts to any child who has suffered an injury. The company also agreed to submit its safety testing protocols to an independent third‑party auditor for the next five years. The DOJ’s action follows a series of complaints from parents and consumer advocacy groups who reported that the toys’ small parts could become lodged in a child’s airway or cause choking.

The settlement is expected to bring closure to the families involved and to reinforce consumer confidence in the toy industry. It also signals the government’s continued focus on product safety, particularly for items marketed to children. The DOJ will monitor XYZ’s compliance with the safety measures and may pursue additional enforcement actions if the company fails to meet its obligations.
author: Euronews

title: Marseille beat Strasbourg 4-0 in Ligue 1 season opener
content:
Algerian international striker Amine Gouiri delivered a decisive performance in the Ligue 1 season opener on Friday evening, netting two second‑half goals as Olympique de Marseille routed Strasbourg 4‑0. The victory, which marked the curtain‑raiser for the new campaign, saw Marseille dominate proceedings from the outset and secure a comfortable lead before Gouiri’s brace sealed the win.

The comprehensive triumph not only gave Marseille three points to start the season but also highlighted their attacking potency ahead of a demanding schedule. With the result, the club positioned itself strongly in the early standings, while Strasbourg were left to regroup after a disappointing debut. The win sets a positive tone for Marseille’s aspirations in the upcoming Ligue 1 season.
author: France 24

title: Australia leads Bangladesh by 101 runs after 18 wickets fall on day one of second Test
content:
Australia surged to a 101‑run advantage over Bangladesh after a dramatic first day of the second Test, propelled by a spectacular spell from their left‑arm bowlers. In the early sessions, left‑arm pacer Josh Hazlewood ripped through the Bangladeshi top order, claiming three wickets for just 22 runs, while fellow left‑arm seamer Mitchell Starc added two more dismissals, including a crucial breakthrough of the number‑four batsman. Bangladesh, bowled out for 215, struggled against the swing and seam movement that the left‑arm attack generated on a seamer‑friendly pitch, leaving them trailing by a sizable margin at stumps.

Australia responded with a solid opening partnership, but the day ended with them at 316 for 4, thanks to a steady 85 from Aaron Finch and a quick‑fire 42 from David Warner. The combination of disciplined bowling and steady batting gave the hosts a commanding 101‑run lead heading into the second day, setting the stage for a potentially decisive contest in the series.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Father leaves 7-year-old son alone on Mount Fuji during hike
content:
A man who was traveling with his two sons reportedly abandoned one of the children during the outing after becoming fatigued, authorities said. The incident, which occurred on a local trail earlier this week, prompted a brief search operation after the boy was discovered missing from the group.

Law enforcement officials confirmed that the remaining child was accounted for and that the father was located and questioned by investigators. The search for the left‑behind boy was called off after it was determined that he had returned to a nearby campsite on his own. The case remains under review to ascertain the circumstances surrounding the abandonment.
author: BBC World

title: South Korea ship to test alternative Arctic route as Mideast conflict disrupts shipping
content: South Korea is scheduled to dispatch its first trial container through the Arctic on Saturday, initiating a strategic pivot in maritime logistics as geopolitical instability forces a reevaluation of global
author: France 24

title: Somalia child hunger crisis deepens after aid cuts, UNICEF says
content:
A drought‑affected country has reported a 32 percent increase in the number of children receiving treatment for severe malnutrition, according to the latest data released by the national health ministry. The rise reflects the worsening food insecurity that has accompanied the prolonged dry season, which has left large swaths of the population without reliable access to adequate nutrition.

The ministry’s figures show that 12,400 children were treated for severe malnutrition in the most recent reporting period, up from 9,400 in the same timeframe last year. Health officials attribute the surge to declining crop yields, disrupted market supply chains, and the displacement of farming communities. In response, the government has expanded mobile clinic services and intensified distribution of therapeutic food packets through partnerships with international aid agencies.

The uptick underscores the urgent need for sustained humanitarian support and long‑term agricultural resilience measures. The ministry has called for increased funding to bolster food security programs and to strengthen early‑warning systems that can better anticipate and mitigate the impact of future drought events.
author: Al Jazeera

title: World Bank Forecasts 6.4% Economic Contraction in Lebanon
content:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned that the recent flare‑up with Israel has stalled Lebanon’s fragile economic recovery, citing a sharp rise in inflation and consumer prices. The short‑term conflict disrupted supply chains, increased the cost of imported goods, and heightened uncertainty among investors and consumers alike. According to the IMF, inflation has climbed to levels that outpace the country’s modest gains from the 2023 recovery plan.

Lebanon’s economy has been in crisis for years, with a banking collapse, a collapsed currency, and a debt burden that exceeds 150 % of GDP. The IMF’s latest assessment notes that the new conflict has amplified these structural weaknesses, pushing food and fuel prices higher and eroding household purchasing power. The agency stresses that without a sustained cease‑fire and a comprehensive economic strategy, the country’s prospects for stabilizing its currency and reducing inflation remain bleak.

In light of these developments, the IMF recommends that Lebanon pursue urgent fiscal and monetary reforms, secure additional international assistance, and work toward a durable political settlement. The agency also urges the government to protect essential imports and support vulnerable households while it navigates the dual challenges of conflict and economic distress.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Libya's Brain Drain Persists 15 Years After Tripoli Fell
content:
Professionals who fled Libya amid the country’s ongoing turmoil say they are unlikely to return, and experts warn that an increasing number of remaining residents may soon follow suit.  In recent months, the capital and other major cities have seen a sharp decline in skilled workers, as the security situation remains volatile and the economy continues to contract.  Many of those who left cite the lack of basic services, the threat of armed groups, and the uncertainty surrounding the national government as key reasons for their decision to stay abroad.

The exodus is affecting critical sectors such as healthcare, engineering, and education, where shortages are already crippling public services.  Analysts note that the loss of experienced professionals could further weaken Libya’s capacity to rebuild infrastructure and provide essential services.  While some returnees hope to resume their careers once stability improves, the prevailing sentiment among the diaspora is that the risk of another wave of violence outweighs the potential benefits of returning home.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Messi fined by MLS for striking opponent in Inter Miami game
content:
Major League Soccer announced on Thursday that Inter Miami will be fined for two separate disciplinary infractions that occurred during the club’s 2‑1 loss to the Philadelphia Union on August 17. Forward Lionel Messi was penalised for “unsporting conduct” after he appeared to exaggerate contact from Union defender Jose Kike Mendoza in the 34th minute, an action the league classified as simulation. The league’s disciplinary committee imposed a $10,000 fine on Messi and issued a formal warning, noting that the incident was reviewed in conjunction with the match officials’ report.

In a separate incident, Inter Miami defender Ian Fray received a $7,500 fine for a “dangerous tackle” on Union midfielder Alejandro Gómez in the 71st minute, which resulted in Gómez being forced to leave the field for treatment. MLS stated that the tackle was deemed a reckless challenge that endangered the safety of an opponent, and the fine reflects the league’s ongoing emphasis on player safety. Both penalties will be recorded on the players’ disciplinary histories, and the league indicated that further violations could result in additional sanctions, including suspensions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Panama Canal to cut daily transits to 32 vessels by September 15
content:
The Panama Canal Authority announced that, effective September 15, the number of daily vessel transits will be reduced from 40 to 32. The decision follows a review of the canal’s capacity and maintenance schedule, which identified that the current throughput is unsustainable without additional upgrades. The cut will affect a wide range of cargo ships, from large container vessels to bulk carriers, potentially extending transit times for global shipping lanes that rely on the canal’s shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans.

The reduction is expected to increase shipping costs for carriers that must reroute around the canal or wait for available slots. Industry analysts predict that the slowdown could add several days to transit times and raise fuel consumption, thereby raising overall freight charges. The Panama Canal Authority has stated that it will monitor traffic closely and will consider further adjustments if traffic volumes exceed the new capacity limits.

In response to the change, shipping companies are reviewing their logistics plans, and some are exploring alternative routes such as the Cape of Good Hope or the proposed Nicaragua Canal. While the canal remains a critical artery for international trade, the temporary reduction in daily transits underscores the need for long‑term infrastructure investment to maintain its competitiveness in an increasingly congested global shipping market.
author: Al Jazeera

title: U.S. imposes 50% tariffs on key Canadian sectors after trade talks collapse
content:
Washington announced on Tuesday that it will impose a 50 percent tariff on a slate of Canadian exports, including lumber, dairy products, and certain agricultural goods, after trade negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed earlier this week. The move, described by the U.S. Trade Representative as a response to what officials called “unfair trade practices” and Canada’s refusal to open its market to American producers, marks the steepest tariff increase on the bilateral relationship in more than two decades. The tariffs will take effect immediately and are expected to raise the cost of the affected Canadian goods in the U.S. market by roughly half, prompting concerns among Canadian exporters and industry groups.

Analysts say the tariffs, while severe, are unlikely to cripple Canada’s overall economy, which remains diversified and heavily integrated with the United States through other trade channels. Canada’s finance ministry projects a modest dip in export revenues for the targeted sectors but expects the broader impact on GDP to be limited, citing strong demand for Canadian energy, technology, and services that are not subject to the new duties. Both governments have signaled a willingness to resume talks, and the imposition of the tariffs may serve as leverage rather than a long‑term policy shift. The situation will be closely monitored as businesses adjust to the new trade landscape and policymakers assess the next steps in the bilateral relationship.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nakashima defeats Fritz, Bejlek upsets Keys in Cincinnati; all‑American semifinal set
content:
Frances Tiafoe and Brandon Nakashima advanced to an all‑American men’s semifinal after both secured victories in the quarterfinal round of the tournament, setting up a domestic showdown for the title. Tiafoe defeated his opponent in straight sets, while Nakashima overcame a first‑set deficit to win in three, each performance underscoring the depth of U.S. talent on the men’s side. In the women’s draw, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula also moved forward, each winning their respective matches to join the later stages of the competition.

The upcoming semifinals will feature Tiafoe versus Nakashima on the men’s side and Gauff against Pegula on the women’s side, promising high‑stakes encounters between the United States’ top players. Both matches are scheduled for the next day, with winners advancing to the finals where they will contend for the championship title. The results highlight a strong showing by American competitors as the tournament approaches its climax.
author: Al Jazeera

title: ‘A brilliant initiative’: the Youth Sport Games goes from strength to strength
content:
Europe’s largest amateur youth sports festival celebrated its 30th anniversary this month in Split, Croatia, drawing a mix of athletes, celebrities and political figures to the Dalmatian coast. The Plazma Youth Sport Games (YSG) – dubbed the “Davos of sport” by some of its high‑profile visitors – hosted finals in ten disciplines, from chess to 3‑v‑3 basketball, over a week of competition. The event attracted just under half a million participants from Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Slovenia and North Macedonia, who had qualified through regional rounds before converging on Split for the grand finale.

A highlight of the chess tournament was a circle of 20 Balkan prodigies playing against grandmaster Nigel Short, who moved a single piece each turn around the group. The children were coached by an eclectic roster of celebrity mentors, including former French Open champion Ana Ivanovic, ex‑Burnley manager Sean Dyche and tech billionaire Peter Thiel, adding a distinctive flair to the matches. Beyond the games, the YSG emphasizes teamwork, collaboration and digital detachment, framing the festival as both a sporting event and a social project aimed at fostering holistic development in young athletes.

As the 30th edition wrapped up, organisers reflected on the festival’s growth and its role in shaping the next generation of European sports talent. The blend of high‑level competition, celebrity engagement and community‑building initiatives underscores Plazma’s continued reputation as a premier platform for youth sport across the region.
author: Guardian Sport

title: African federations eye Grafström to challenge Infantino
content:
African football federations have reportedly approached Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, to gauge his willingness to oppose Gianni Infantino’s bid for re‑election as president. According to the Guardian, up to fifteen national associations across the continent are prepared to withdraw their support for Infantino if he seeks another term next year, signalling a potential shift in the continent’s stance on the governing body’s leadership.

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) maintains that its executive committee has “unanimously reconfirmed” backing for the 56‑year‑old president, a claim that stands in contrast to the emerging reports of dissent. While CAF’s position underscores continued loyalty, the outreach to Grafström suggests that senior African officials are exploring alternatives that could reshape the power dynamics within Fifa, particularly if Infantino’s re‑election is contested.

If the outreach to Grafström proves fruitful, it could mark a significant realignment in Fifa’s governance, potentially influencing the organization’s future policies and the representation of African football on the global stage. The outcome will depend on the responses from both Grafström and Infantino as the election cycle approaches.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Ødegaard Returns to Arsenal as Playmaker After Injury
content:
Arsenal captain Gabriel Jesus has shown early signs of recovery from a season‑long injury crisis, scoring a goal that reminded fans of the playful spirit of “It’s A Knockout” during a recent friendly. The striker’s return comes after a campaign that saw him miss a significant portion of matches, and his performance has been hailed as a positive indicator ahead of the club’s Premier League opener.

The club’s preparations have been highlighted by Sky Sports, which announced it will broadcast a total of 1,500 live games this season, amounting to roughly 3,000 hours of coverage. This extensive schedule underscores the broadcaster’s commitment to delivering comprehensive football content, while Arsenal’s focus remains on regaining full fitness and momentum for the start of the campaign.

With the new season on the horizon, Arsenal’s management and supporters will be watching closely to see if Jesus can maintain his form and help the team secure a strong position in the league standings. The club’s recovery efforts and the extensive broadcast coverage set the stage for a highly anticipated Premier League season.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Premier League opening day: Hull vs Manchester United preview and new transfers
content:
The Premier League kicked off its new campaign with a decisive opening‑day clash, as Arsenal delivered a comprehensive 4‑0 victory over Coventry City. The Gunners’ performance, highlighted by a clean sheet and a dominant possession game, underscored their intent to return to the upper echelons of the table after a challenging previous season.

Fixtures for the week have drawn attention to several emerging talents and new signings across the league. Analysts and fans alike are keen to see how fresh faces will fit into their respective squads, with predicted line‑ups suggesting a mix of experienced leaders and promising prospects. The focus on these new players reflects the clubs’ strategies to strengthen depth and inject fresh energy into their campaigns.

As the Premier League resumes, the spotlight remains on how teams adapt to the return of full‑strength rosters and how newly signed players will influence match outcomes. The opening fixtures set the tone for the season, offering a glimpse into the tactical adjustments and player performances that will shape the league’s narrative moving forward.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Amanda Serrano's 50th win garners over 3 million TikTok views
content:
Amanda Serrano secured her 50th career victory when she defeated Argentine boxer Lucrecia Manzur in a highly anticipated bout that took place on June 15, 2026, at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas. The fight, part of the WBC’s “World Boxing Showcase,” saw Serrano use a combination of sharp jab work and powerful counterpunches to dominate the contest, earning a unanimous decision from the judges. The match was broadcast live on several platforms, including a dedicated TikTok livestream that attracted more than three million viewers worldwide, underscoring the growing influence of social media in promoting professional boxing.

The win marks a significant milestone in Serrano’s career, as she becomes the first female boxer to reach 50 professional victories while maintaining an undefeated record in her weight class. The bout also highlighted the rising popularity of women's boxing, with Manzur’s performance praised for her resilience and technical skill. As Serrano celebrates this achievement, analysts note that her continued success could pave the way for increased visibility and sponsorship opportunities for female fighters in the sport.
author: BBC Sport

title: Russian strikes kill at least two in Ukraine, injure several
content:
At least two people were reported dead early Saturday, local authorities said, after a new wave of Russian strikes hit Ukrainian territory. The casualties were confirmed in the aftermath of air and missile attacks that targeted residential areas and infrastructure, adding to the toll of recent hostilities in the region.

The Saturday attacks followed a series of bombings on Friday that killed at least 20 people, including 16 victims of a daytime drone strike on a crowded shopping centre in Kryvyi Rih, the hometown of President Volodymyr Zelensky. Ukrainian officials have condemned the escalations, while international observers continue to monitor the situation amid ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine.
author: France 24

title: Court hears Lindsay Clancy experienced command hallucinations during child killings
content:
In a pivotal moment of the ongoing murder trial, the defense called its final witness—a forensic psychiatrist—to the stand on Tuesday. The specialist was tasked with explaining the clinical characteristics of postpartum psychosis, a rare but severe mental‑health condition that can emerge in the weeks following childbirth and is associated with hallucinations, delusions, and extreme mood disturbances. By detailing how the disorder can impair judgment and reality testing, the psychiatrist aimed to establish a link between the defendant’s recent postpartum period and the alleged criminal conduct.

The testimony, which lasted approximately forty minutes, included references to diagnostic criteria, typical symptom trajectories, and the potential for sudden, impulsive actions driven by psychotic episodes. Prosecutors cross‑examined the expert on the rarity of violent behavior among postpartum psychosis patients and on the availability of treatment options. The court will now consider the psychiatrist’s insights alongside other evidence before delivering a verdict, with the judge slated to issue a ruling later this month.
author: BBC World

title: Cris Cyborg’s title not at stake after Ketlen Vieira misses weight
content:
Cris “Cyborg” Justino’s feather‑weight world title bout at the Professional Fighters League (PFL) event in Tampa on Saturday will no longer be contested for the championship after her scheduled opponent, Ketlen Vieira, failed to make the required weight limit. The fight, originally billed as a title defense for the Brazilian veteran, will proceed as a non‑title bout following the weigh‑in results.

PFL officials confirmed that Vieira’s excess weight disqualified the contest from being a championship match, and the organization will enforce the standard penalties for missing weight, including a fine and a portion of her purse being awarded to Cyborg. The change does not affect the fighters’ contracts or the overall card, and the bout will still be featured as part of the league’s regular season schedule.
author: BBC Sport

title: UK recycling centres lose £1bn annually to lithium battery fires
content:
Experts report that fires ignited by improperly discarded lithium batteries—commonly found in vapes—are now occurring at waste facilities at a rate exceeding ten incidents per week. The new figures highlight a growing safety concern as these battery‑related blazes threaten the lives of workers and nearby residents.

The volume of such fires has reached a crisis level, according to fire safety specialists, with annual costs estimated at £1 billion. Fire chiefs have expressed frustration over the frequency and severity of the incidents, noting that the rapid spread of lithium‑battery fires complicates emergency response and increases the risk of injury and property damage.

Authorities are reviewing current disposal regulations and encouraging stricter compliance to curb the trend. The situation underscores the need for improved public awareness and more robust waste‑management protocols for high‑energy batteries.
author: Guardian Environment

title: OpenAI cuts GPT‑5.6 Sol price by 20%
content:
OpenAI has announced the launch of a new language model, GPT‑5.6, which is now available through its API. The update, detailed on the company’s developer documentation site, introduces a “sol” variant that offers refined performance on a range of natural‑language tasks, including text generation, summarization, and code synthesis. According to the release notes, GPT‑5.6 builds on the architecture of its predecessor, GPT‑5, with optimizations that reduce inference latency and improve context handling for longer prompts.

The model is positioned as a drop‑in replacement for earlier versions, with developers encouraged to test it against their existing workloads. OpenAI highlights that GPT‑5.6 achieves higher accuracy on benchmark datasets such as MMLU and OpenBookQA, while also incorporating enhanced safety mitigations to curb hallucinations and reduce bias. The announcement has sparked discussion on Hacker News, where the post has attracted 38 up‑votes and 20 comments, with users evaluating the practical gains in performance and the cost implications of adopting the new model.

While the exact pricing tier for GPT‑5.6 remains to be confirmed, the release underscores OpenAI’s ongoing commitment to iterative improvements in its language models. The company has stated that the new variant will be available to all API customers in the coming weeks, and it is expected to influence a broad spectrum of applications—from conversational agents to automated content creation—by providing more reliable and contextually aware outputs.
author: Hacker News

title: Canada to Match US Tariffs Dollar for Dollar, Says Finance Minister
content:
Toronto – In recent weeks, Canada has moved forward in negotiations aimed at securing what officials describe as “the best deal in the world” with the United States, according to Mark Carney, former governor of the Bank of Canada and current special envoy on trade. Carney highlighted a series of incremental agreements on tariffs, regulatory alignment, and cross‑border investment that have narrowed gaps identified in earlier rounds of talks. The advances, he noted, reflect a concerted effort by both governments to strengthen economic ties and address lingering issues such as agricultural market access and digital trade provisions.

Despite the progress, Carney cautioned that the gains fall short of the objectives set for Canadian stakeholders. He emphasized that the current trajectory does not fully meet the expectations for job creation, price stability, and broader economic benefits that were outlined at the outset of the negotiations. The statement underscores the need for further dialogue and potential concessions before a final agreement can be ratified, signaling that while momentum exists, additional work remains to align the deal with Canada’s strategic priorities.
author: Euronews

title: Panama Canal to Reduce Daily Ship Transits Starting September
content:
The Panama Canal Authority announced that the waterway will reduce its daily ship transits beginning in September as persistent low rainfall and an intensifying El Niño event diminish reservoir levels. The cutback, which will lower the maximum number of vessels allowed to cross each day, is intended to conserve water while maintaining safe navigation standards across the canal’s locks.

Officials indicated that the reduction will remain in effect until water levels stabilize, with the authority monitoring rainfall and reservoir data on a weekly basis. The adjustment is expected to affect global shipping schedules, prompting carriers to consider alternative routes or adjust cargo loads. The canal, which handles roughly 5 percent of world trade, emphasized that the measure is a temporary response to the climatic conditions and that operations will resume normal capacity once sufficient water is restored.
author: DW World

title: Assam floods cause multiple deaths and missing persons
content:
Heavy rains over the past week have turned rivers into raging torrents across the [region], prompting emergency services to launch large‑scale rescue operations and leaving a growing death toll in their wake. Local officials confirmed that dozens of people have been killed or remain missing, with floodwaters inundating homes, roads and critical infrastructure. Among the victims, a father continues to search for the body of his 8‑year‑old daughter, while another resident lost his life after drowning while attempting to pull a friend from the swollen creek.

Authorities have deployed helicopters, boats and ground crews to evacuate stranded residents and to recover bodies, while shelters have been set up for thousands of displaced families. The disaster response team warned that rising water levels could persist for several more days, urging communities to heed evacuation orders and avoid entering flood‑affected zones. As recovery efforts intensify, officials say the full extent of the damage will be assessed in the coming weeks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: China launches Chang'e-7 mission to study lunar ice
content:
China’s upcoming lunar probe, Chang’e‑7, is slated to launch later this year with the primary objective of investigating water ice deposits in the Moon’s permanently shadowed craters. The spacecraft will enter a low‑altitude polar orbit, allowing its suite of spectrometers, radar, and thermal imagers to map the distribution and abundance of volatiles within the permanently dark regions of the lunar south pole. By conducting in‑situ measurements and high‑resolution remote sensing, the mission aims to quantify the quantity of water trapped in regolith and assess its accessibility for future exploration.
