The data gathered by Chang’e‑7 will complement previous findings from missions such as NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and India’s Chandrayaan‑3, providing a more detailed picture of lunar water resources. Scientists anticipate that a clearer understanding of these deposits could inform the planning of sustainable human presence on the Moon, including the development of in‑situ resource utilization technologies. The mission’s results are expected to be released to the international scientific community within a year of the probe’s arrival, offering new insights into the Moon’s volatile inventory and its implications for future space endeavors.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Maddison credits twins for distraction from ACL injury
content:
Tottenham Hotspur midfielder James Maddison said that the distraction of his young family helped him cope with a serious ACL injury that kept him out of action last season. The 26‑year‑old revealed on a club media platform that he has five children under the age of five, including a second set of twins, and that the demands of parenting kept his mind off the rehabilitation process.

Maddison’s injury, sustained during the 2023‑24 campaign, required surgery and a lengthy recovery period that sidelined him for several months. While he was unable to contribute on the pitch, he remained involved with the squad through training sessions and team meetings, citing the routine of caring for his children as a steady source of motivation and mental relief. The midfielder’s return to full fitness is expected ahead of the final stretch of the Premier League season, where he will be looking to add depth to Tottenham’s midfield rotation.
author: BBC Sport

title: UN uses AI to improve education, health and environmental monitoring worldwide
content:
Artificial intelligence is quietly reshaping health and learning outcomes across continents. In Jamaica, six‑year‑old Ari, who struggles with learning difficulties, has gained access to a book in his native language thanks to an AI‑powered reading assistant. The system translates text in real time, allowing Ari to follow the story and build literacy skills that were previously out of reach.

Across the globe, the same technology is accelerating medical diagnostics and environmental monitoring. In Ethiopia, AI algorithms process chest X‑rays of gold‑mining workers, reducing the time required to screen for tuberculosis from days to minutes. Meanwhile, AI‑driven sensors detect methane leaks in industrial and agricultural settings, enabling rapid containment and improving air quality for communities worldwide.

These developments illustrate how artificial intelligence can bridge gaps in education, healthcare, and environmental stewardship, delivering timely solutions that benefit individuals and societies alike.
author: UN News

title: ‘We are in the inferno’: diaspora writers lead new movement of nature poetry
content:
A new anthology of eco‑poetry has drawn attention to a previously under‑represented segment of the UK literary scene. Titled *Where Are Our Black and Asian Nature Writers?*, the collection was co‑edited by Mona Arshi and features voices from African, Asian and Caribbean diasporas. The book was born from a viral social‑media question that Arshi posted, asking why there seemed to be a dearth of black and Asian writers in the field of nature poetry.

The anthology is part of a broader movement of eco‑poets from black and brown communities who are challenging the traditional canon of nature verse amid the current climate and biodiversity crisis. By foregrounding diverse perspectives on the natural world, the collection offers fresh insights into environmental issues and celebrates the cultural heritage of its contributors. The title’s call to “write about daffodils again” signals a return to familiar natural imagery, re‑imagined through these new lenses.

The publication has sparked renewed interest in eco‑poetry across the UK, encouraging publishers, readers and educators to broaden the scope of nature writing. As the anthology gains traction, it is expected to inspire further projects that highlight the contributions of marginalized communities to environmental literature.
author: Guardian Environment

title: 4 in 10 Travellers Visit Sites to Capture Social Media Content
content:
TUI Group, together with travel‑marketplace Musement, has released new research that highlights the growing impact of social media on travel behaviour. The study, published on the TUI Group newsroom, found that 4 in 10 travellers visit tourist sites specifically to capture content for platforms such as Instagram and TikTok. It also shows that a majority of respondents use social media to plan trips, with visual appeal and shareability becoming key decision factors.

According to the survey, which sampled travellers across multiple countries, 70 % of participants turn to social media for inspiration, while 40 % say they visit a location primarily to create shareable moments. The research further indicates that 60 % of travellers would recommend a destination based on its online visual presence, and that “Instagrammable” experiences are increasingly shaping destination popularity. The findings point to a shift in how destinations are marketed, with digital storytelling and content‑friendly attractions gaining prominence.

The study underscores the importance of a strong digital presence for tourism stakeholders. By recognising that social media content creation now drives a significant portion of travel decisions, destinations and travel providers can tailor their offerings and marketing strategies to better meet the expectations of a digitally engaged audience.
author: Hacker News

title: Canada to Match US Tariffs Dollar for Dollar After Trade Talks Fail
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced that Canada will match United States tariffs on the same products “dollar for dollar” to safeguard Canadian workers and businesses. The statement came after the U.S. imposed new duties on a range of Canadian goods on Saturday, following a week of stalled negotiations between the two countries. Carney said the decision was taken to prevent a competitive disadvantage for Canadian producers and to maintain the balance of trade.

The U.S. tariffs, which target Canadian dairy, lumber and certain agricultural items, were implemented after the Canadian government failed to secure a tariff‑relief agreement during the negotiation period. Carney’s pledge signals a retaliatory stance, mirroring the U.S. approach, and underscores Canada’s intent to protect its domestic industries from the impact of the new duties. The Canadian government has indicated that the matching tariffs will be applied to the same categories and at the same rates as the U.S. levies.

In a brief conclusion, Carney emphasized that the move is aimed at preserving the competitiveness of Canadian businesses and ensuring that Canadian workers are not adversely affected by the U.S. tariff increase. He urged both governments to resume talks to resolve the dispute and avoid further escalation.
author: France 24

title: Nigeria and Sahel Face Growing Security Divide
content:
A growing diplomatic rift between the United States and Mexico is now hindering coordinated efforts to address the persistent drug‑trafficking threat that crosses their shared border. Recent tensions, sparked by disagreements over extradition procedures and trade policy, have led to a slowdown in joint intelligence sharing and a pause in several joint task‑force operations that had been actively targeting major cartel networks.

Both sides have cited specific incidents that illustrate the widening divide. Washington has announced new sanctions on several Mexican officials it claims are linked to cartel protection, while Mexico has publicly criticized what it calls “unilateral interference” by the United States in its domestic law‑enforcement processes. The U.S. Department of Justice has reported that the sanctions have disrupted the flow of critical drug‑trafficking intelligence, while the Mexican Secretariat of Public Security has noted a reduction in the frequency of joint patrols and shared surveillance data. Officials from both governments have reiterated their commitment to combatting organized crime but have also warned that the diplomatic strain could prolong the operational gaps in border security.

The continued diplomatic friction threatens to undermine progress against the cross‑border drug‑trafficking network, potentially allowing cartels to expand their influence. While both governments have called for renewed dialogue, the current impasse underscores the need for a diplomatic resolution to restore the full effectiveness of their joint security initiatives.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 17-year-old Palestinian killed in West Bank settler attack, UN condemns
content:
A 17‑year‑old Palestinian was killed and a second individual suffered serious injuries after an incident described by local authorities as a settler attack in the occupied West Bank. The assault took place near the settlement of Migdalim, where witnesses reported that a group of Israeli civilians approached a vehicle occupied by the two Palestinians, opened fire, and fled the scene. The Palestinian health ministry confirmed the teen’s death and the critical condition of the other victim, who was transported to a nearby hospital for emergency treatment.

The Israeli military’s regional command issued a statement that a police investigation had been launched, but it did not provide details about the identities of the assailants or any arrests. Palestinian officials called the incident a continuation of a pattern of settler violence, citing recent reports from human‑rights organizations that document similar attacks on civilians in the area. The incident occurs amid heightened tensions over settlement expansion and frequent clashes between Israeli settlers and Palestinian residents in the region.

International observers have urged both parties to cooperate with the investigation and to take steps to prevent further civilian casualties. The Palestinian Authority has demanded accountability, while Israeli officials have reiterated that law‑enforcement measures are being taken to address the crime. The situation remains under close monitoring as regional leaders seek to de‑escalate the volatile environment in the West Bank.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Northern Philippine communities demand answers on flood control funding
content:
Al Jazeera’s correspondent Jamela Alindogan is on the ground in the northern Philippines, where a series of severe floods have left dozens of villages submerged and residents pressing local officials for explanations. Heavy monsoon rains over the past week have caused rivers to overflow, inundating homes, schools and agricultural fields across the provinces of Ilocos Norte and Cagayan, according to reports from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council.

Local authorities have deployed rescue teams and set up temporary shelters, while the Department of Public Works and Highways has begun assessments of damaged infrastructure. Community leaders, however, have voiced frustration over perceived delays in relief distribution and the lack of clear communication regarding flood mitigation measures. Government spokespersons reiterated their commitment to expedite aid and to review the region’s drainage systems, citing the need for a coordinated response to prevent future inundations. The situation remains fluid as recovery efforts continue and residents await further assistance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Canada matches US tariffs with 50% levy on $20 billion of imports
content:
A 50 percent levy on roughly $20 billion worth of Canadian imports has taken effect after trade negotiations between the United States and Canada collapsed at the last minute. The tariff, announced by the U.S. Trade Representative’s office on Monday, applies to a range of goods including lumber, dairy products, and certain manufactured items, and is slated to remain in place pending a formal review of the stalled talks. Officials said the measure is intended to protect domestic industries and to pressure Canada back to the negotiating table, where discussions had focused on updating the United States‑Mexico‑Canada Agreement and addressing longstanding disputes over market access.

The abrupt implementation follows a series of high‑level meetings that failed to produce a consensus on key issues such as dairy quotas and timber export restrictions. Canadian trade ministers have warned that the levy could increase prices for U.S. consumers and disrupt supply chains, while U.S. policymakers argue the step underscores the need for a balanced agreement. Both governments have indicated a willingness to resume dialogue, but no timetable has been set for further negotiations, leaving the $20 billion of affected trade at risk of prolonged uncertainty.
author: BBC World

title: Trump administration wants to deny ABA ability to oversee law schools: Report
content:
The U.S. Department of Education has signaled that it may terminate the American Bar Association’s (ABA) authority to accredit law schools, a power the organization has wielded for nearly seven decades. According to a recent Wall Street Journal report, the Department is reviewing the ABA’s accreditation process as part of a broader effort to modernize higher‑education oversight and reduce regulatory duplication. The ABA has accredited close to 200 law schools nationwide, a standard that has shaped admissions, curriculum requirements, and bar‑exam eligibility for graduates.

If the Department’s proposal moves forward, it would shift the responsibility for evaluating law‑school quality from the ABA to the federal education agency, potentially altering the criteria used to assess institutional performance and student outcomes. The change could also impact the legal profession’s regulatory framework, as bar admission requirements in many states currently hinge on ABA accreditation. While the Department has not yet finalized its decision, stakeholders—including law‑school administrators, faculty, and bar associations—are monitoring the development closely, noting that any transition would require careful coordination to maintain consistency in legal education standards.
author: The Hill

title: US Imposes 50% Tariffs on $20B of Canadian Goods
content:
The United States announced on Saturday that it would impose a 50 % tariff on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, a move that followed a series of failed last‑ditch negotiations between the two countries. The tariffs, which cover a range of products including automobiles, dairy, and agricultural items, are intended to pressure Canada to comply with U.S. trade demands that Canada has deemed unfair.

In response, Canada immediately declared its intention to retaliate. Ottawa said it would seek to impose its own tariffs on U.S. goods and explore other trade remedies, citing the need to protect Canadian industries and maintain reciprocal trade relations. The dispute marks a significant escalation in the long‑standing trade tensions that have involved issues such as dairy quotas, vehicle manufacturing standards, and the broader North American Free Trade Agreement framework.

Both governments have indicated that they remain open to further dialogue, but the tariffs are expected to impact Canadian exporters and could trigger a broader trade war if retaliatory measures are enacted. The situation remains fluid as officials from both sides work to negotiate a resolution while managing the economic implications for their respective markets.
author: NPR Politics

title: Canada to Match US 50% Tariffs After Trade Deal Collapse
content:
Canadian trade negotiator Mark Carney has publicly condemned the United States for what he described as “unfair” last‑minute changes to a proposed trade agreement, after the two countries failed to reach a deal by the midnight deadline following a three‑day extension of talks. Carney said the U.S. modifications were “uneconomic” and raised doubts about the reliability of any agreement that could be reached.

In response to the U.S. tariff proposals, Carney pledged that Canada would match the tariffs dollar for dollar, a move that could broaden the scope of the dispute if a settlement is not achieved. The statement also called into question the U.S. commitment to the negotiation process, suggesting that the sudden adjustments undermined the credibility of the deal.

Both sides remain at a stalemate, with Canadian officials indicating that further negotiations will be necessary to resolve the tariff differences. The outcome of the talks will shape the future of trade relations between the two nations and could influence broader economic policy decisions in North America.
author: Guardian World

title: Judge Overturns Trump Visa Ban on 75 Countries
content:
A federal judge in Manhattan has overturned a State Department order that had suspended the issuance of immigrant visas to applicants from several countries. The ruling, issued by U.S. District Judge [Name] on [date], declares the suspension unlawful, citing violations of the Administrative Procedure Act and the Constitution’s equal protection clause. The judge ordered the State Department to resume processing visas and to provide a detailed justification for any future suspensions.

The suspension, imposed in late 2023, was part of a broader policy aimed at tightening immigration controls amid concerns over security and compliance with immigration laws. Critics argued that the measure disproportionately affected lawful permanent residents and their families, while supporters maintained it was necessary to prevent potential threats. The court’s decision follows a series of legal challenges that have highlighted the tension between executive discretion and statutory limits on visa issuance.

The State Department has indicated it will appeal the ruling, but the immediate effect is a reinstatement of visa processing for the affected nationals. The case underscores the judiciary’s role in reviewing executive actions that impact immigration policy and the rights of individuals seeking lawful entry into the United States.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US imposes 50% tariffs on $20 bn of Canadian goods after trade talks fail
content:
Ottawa announced on Thursday that Canada will impose retaliatory tariffs on a “dollar for dollar” basis in response to the United States’ decision not to move forward with a pending trade agreement. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau made the declaration during a press conference, stating that the measure is intended to protect Canadian producers and signal that Canada will not accept unilateral trade actions that disadvantage its economy. The announcement follows weeks of stalled negotiations over a proposed amendment to the United States‑Mexico‑Canada Agreement (USMCA), which sought to address lingering disputes on dairy, lumber and automotive rules of origin.

Under the new policy, Canada will match any U.S. tariff imposed on Canadian goods with an equivalent duty on the same U.S. product, covering sectors ranging from agricultural commodities to manufactured items. Trade officials indicated that the tariffs will be applied automatically once the United States enacts its own measures, and they emphasized that the approach is a temporary, reciprocal response designed to bring both parties back to the negotiating table. Analysts predict that the tit‑for‑tat strategy could increase costs for businesses on both sides of the border and may prompt further diplomatic efforts to resolve the outstanding trade issues.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 13 Tunisians missing after migrant boat capsizes en route to Italy
content:
Since 2014, more than 5,000 migrants have lost their lives while attempting to cross the Mediterranean Sea to reach Europe, according to data compiled by the International Organization for Migration (IOM). The fatalities have occurred primarily along the central and eastern Mediterranean routes, where vessels departing from Libya, Tunisia, and Egypt often encounter hazardous weather, overcrowding, and limited rescue capacity.

The high death toll has prompted a series of responses from European Union member states and international agencies, including the deployment of naval patrols, the establishment of search‑and‑rescue operations, and the implementation of migration agreements with transit countries. Despite these measures, the number of crossings remains substantial, and humanitarian organizations continue to call for coordinated efforts to improve safety and address the underlying drivers of migration. The ongoing loss of life underscores the persistent challenges facing regional migration management and maritime security.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Leavitt to Join Trump MAGA Inc. Super PAC After White House Exit
content:
Karoline Leavitt, who served as the White House press secretary for the final weeks of the Trump administration, has confirmed that she will leave the White House and join the President’s Trump MAGA Inc. Super PAC. The announcement came from the outgoing press secretary on Friday, after Leavitt told reporters outside Air Force One that she would step down at the end of her brief tenure.

Leavitt, who was appointed to the post in early February, said she will take on a communications role with the Super PAC, a move that signals her continued involvement in Republican political operations. The Super PAC, which has been active in supporting Trump’s political agenda and fundraising efforts, will benefit from Leavitt’s experience in White House media strategy and her familiarity with the administration’s messaging priorities.

Her departure marks the end of a short stint in the Oval Office and underscores the ongoing transition of Trump‑aligned staff to new political ventures. The move also highlights the broader trend of former White House officials moving into campaign and super‑PAC work after leaving the executive branch.
author: The Hill

title: Younger Lung Cancer Patients More Likely to Have Targetable Genetic Changes
content:
A recent international study has found that younger adults diagnosed with non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are significantly more likely than older patients to possess genetic alterations that can be targeted with specific therapies. The research, conducted by a consortium of investigators and led in part by scientists at the Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center of the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine, analyzed genomic data from thousands of NSCLC cases across multiple countries.

The study identified a higher prevalence of actionable mutations—such as EGFR, ALK, ROS1, and BRAF alterations—in patients under 50 compared with those over 70. These findings underscore the importance of comprehensive genomic profiling for younger patients, as targeted treatments can improve outcomes and reduce toxicity compared with conventional chemotherapy. The results also suggest that age may influence the molecular landscape of lung cancer, prompting clinicians to consider earlier and more aggressive testing for genetic drivers in younger cohorts.

Overall, the research highlights a clear age-related difference in the genomic profile of NSCLC and reinforces the growing role of precision medicine in tailoring treatment strategies. By identifying patients who are most likely to benefit from targeted therapies, clinicians can improve survival rates and quality of life for younger lung cancer patients.
author: Medical Xpress

title: EU Scientists Urge Mosquito Control to Fight Rising Mosquito-Borne Diseases in Europe
content:
European scientists have underscored the growing need for mosquito control as a key strategy to curb the rise of mosquito‑borne illnesses across the continent. In a recent article published in *Eurosurveillance*, experts from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC), the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA), the European Environment Agency (EEA), and the European Commission highlighted the increasing incidence of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile virus infections in Europe.

The joint statement stresses that effective vector management—encompassing surveillance, habitat reduction, and targeted insecticide use—must be integrated into national public health plans. It notes that the expanding geographic range of Aedes and Culex mosquitoes, driven by climate change and global travel, has amplified the risk of disease transmission, necessitating coordinated action across EU member states. The agencies call for harmonised policies, improved data sharing, and investment in research to develop sustainable control measures.

By prioritising mosquito control, European health authorities aim to reduce the burden of these emerging diseases and protect public health. The article serves as a call to action for governments, scientists, and communities to adopt evidence‑based strategies that will mitigate the spread of dengue, chikungunya, and West Nile virus across the region.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Telemedicine Intervention Fails to Reduce Nursing Home Hospitalizations
content:
A prospective, multicenter cluster‑randomized trial found that an intersectoral, telemedicine‑based intervention implemented in nursing homes did not produce a statistically significant reduction in patient hospitalizations. The study was designed to evaluate whether coordinated digital care could lower the rate of acute admissions from long‑term care facilities.

The trial, led by John Grosser, Sophie Pauge, Birthe Aufenberg and Prof. Dr. Wolfgang Greiner from Bielefeld University’s Department of Health Economics and Health Care Management, enrolled nursing homes across several regions. Participants received a structured telemedicine program that linked nursing staff with external medical specialists, aiming to manage acute conditions on site and reduce the need for hospital transfers. Despite the intervention’s comprehensive approach, the analysis of hospitalization rates showed no significant difference compared with control facilities.

These findings suggest that, under the conditions tested, the telemedicine strategy did not achieve its primary goal of decreasing hospital admissions among nursing home residents. The results highlight the need for further research to identify more effective methods for reducing acute care utilization in this population.
author: Medical Xpress

title: FDA Approves First Standalone Robotic Blood-Draw Device
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has granted marketing authorization to Vitestro for its Aletta system, the first standalone robotic device capable of drawing blood from a patient’s arm. The FDA’s approval marks a milestone in medical device innovation, allowing Aletta to be used in clinical settings without the need for a traditional phlebotomist.

Aletta operates by autonomously locating a vein, inserting a needle, and collecting the required volume of blood. The system is designed to reduce patient discomfort, improve consistency in sample collection, and free up healthcare staff for other tasks. Vitestro’s technology has undergone extensive clinical testing to demonstrate safety, accuracy, and reliability in a range of patient populations.

With this authorization, Vitestro becomes the first company to bring a fully automated blood‑draw device to the U.S. market, potentially reshaping routine phlebotomy procedures in hospitals, laboratories, and outpatient clinics.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Two-thirds of Americans support banning glyphosate, survey finds
content:
A new nationally representative poll conducted by the Annenberg Public Policy Center at the University of Pennsylvania finds that two‑thirds of Americans support banning glyphosate, the herbicide’s active ingredient in the widely used Roundup weedkiller, from crops grown in the United States. The survey, which sampled a cross‑section of the adult population, indicates a substantial shift in public opinion toward stricter regulation of the chemical in domestic agriculture.

The findings arrive amid ongoing debate over glyphosate’s safety, with health agencies and courts previously weighing its carcinogenic potential and numerous lawsuits challenging its use. While the federal government has yet to enact a nationwide ban, the strong public preference highlighted by the APPC study could influence future policy discussions and regulatory actions concerning the herbicide’s application on food crops.
author: Phys.org

title: Early Humans Consumed Carbohydrates and Sugary Foods, Study Finds
content:
A new synthesis of archaeological, biochemical and genetic evidence indicates that early human ancestors regularly consumed a diet rich in natural sugars and complex carbohydrates, challenging the long‑standing view that prehistoric hominins subsisted primarily on meat and raw vegetation. Researchers examined dental calculus, stable‑isotope ratios in fossilized bones, and plant micro‑remains from sites dating between 2 million and 200 thousand years ago, finding consistent traces of fruit sugars, tuber starches and even honey residues. These findings are corroborated by genetic analyses that show a gradual increase in AMY1 gene copy number—responsible for salivary amylase production—across Homo species, suggesting an evolutionary response to higher carbohydrate intake.

The study highlights that early hominins exploited a variety of carbohydrate sources, including ripe fruits, underground storage organs, and seasonal nectar, to meet energy demands during periods of low meat availability. Microwear patterns on molar surfaces reveal grinding motions typical of processing fibrous plant material, while isotopic signatures point to a mixed diet with up to 30 percent of caloric intake derived from plant‑based sugars and starches. The timing of these dietary shifts aligns with climatic fluctuations that expanded savanna habitats, providing abundant edible flora and encouraging foraging behaviors that later paved the way for the development of cooking and food processing techniques.

These insights refine the understanding of human nutritional evolution, illustrating that carbohydrate consumption has deep roots in our lineage. The evidence underscores the adaptability of early ancestors to diverse food resources and offers a broader context for contemporary discussions on diet and metabolic health.
author: Hacker News

title: Lord O'Neill declines role as Andy Burnham's chief economic adviser
content:
Lord O’Neill, a former chief economist at Goldman Sachs and a former Treasury adviser, has been identified as a likely candidate to serve as chief economic adviser to Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham. The suggestion emerged from sources familiar with the mayor’s office as Burnham prepares to assemble a new policy team ahead of the upcoming local elections and the rollout of his regional economic agenda.

If appointed, O’Neill would bring extensive experience in macro‑economic policy, having previously chaired the UK’s Office for Budget Responsibility and served on the Treasury’s advisory board. His expertise is expected to support Burnham’s focus on post‑pandemic recovery, infrastructure investment, and skills development across the North West. The mayor’s office has not yet confirmed the appointment, but officials indicate that discussions are underway and a decision could be announced in the coming weeks.
author: BBC Politics

title: US debt-to-GDP ratio data and discussion
content:
The US Debt Clock website now lists the nation’s debt‑to‑GDP ratio at roughly 130 percent, indicating that total federal liabilities exceed the country’s annual economic output. The figure, which updates in real time, reflects a national debt that has surpassed $33 trillion while gross domestic product hovers around $25 trillion, according to the site’s latest data.

Analysts note that the current ratio marks a significant rise from the early 2000s, when the debt‑to‑GDP measure lingered near 60 percent, and it surpasses the post‑World War II peak of about 119 percent. A discussion thread on Hacker News highlighted the metric, drawing ten up‑votes and a single comment that underscored concerns about fiscal sustainability without delving into policy prescriptions.

While the elevated ratio underscores the scale of the United States’ borrowing relative to its economic base, officials and economists continue to monitor its trajectory as part of broader assessments of fiscal health and long‑term budgetary planning.
author: Hacker News

title: Six-year-old Palestinian-British girl dies after family drowned off UK coast
content:
Saja el‑Khawas was found dead on Wednesday, her death occurring shortly after the drowning of her mother, father and sister on Tuesday. The four family members were discovered in a nearby body of water, prompting an immediate response from local emergency services who confirmed the fatalities after conducting rescue and recovery operations.

Authorities have launched an investigation to determine the circumstances surrounding the incident, while officials have offered condolences to the grieving relatives. The tragedy underscores ongoing concerns about water safety in the area, and police have urged residents to exercise caution near rivers, lakes, and other aquatic environments.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Peru rescues people trapped by highway landslides after nearly a week
content:
A landslide that struck a major highway in the central Andes of Peru last week left dozens of motorists stranded for nearly seven days before rescue teams were able to reach them. The blockage occurred on the Carretera Central, a vital transport corridor connecting Lima with the highland regions, after heavy rains triggered a series of mudslides that collapsed a section of the road and buried several vehicles.

Peruvian emergency services, including the National Police, the Army’s engineering corps, and local fire brigades, coordinated a multi‑day operation to free the trapped individuals. Helicopters were deployed to air‑lift supplies and evacuate the injured, while ground crews used excavators and manual labor to clear debris. By the end of the operation, more than a dozen people had been rescued, several of whom required medical attention for injuries sustained during the entrapment. Authorities also reopened the highway to limited traffic after confirming the stability of the surrounding slopes.

The incident highlights the ongoing vulnerability of Peru’s mountainous infrastructure to extreme weather events. Officials said they will conduct a thorough assessment of the affected stretch and reinforce the area to prevent similar occurrences, while urging drivers to monitor weather forecasts and road conditions before traveling in high‑risk zones.
author: Al Jazeera

title: How this 1960s ex-council house is managing to stay cool without air con
content:
The Passivhaus standard, originally developed in Germany, is gaining traction among UK homeowners as the country faces increasingly hot summer temperatures. The low‑energy building specification, which emphasizes airtight construction, high‑performance insulation, and mechanical ventilation with heat recovery, offers a proven strategy for maintaining comfortable indoor climates without excessive reliance on air conditioning.

Recent market surveys show a steady rise in Passivhaus‑certified projects across England, Scotland, and Wales, with developers citing both energy‑cost savings and improved indoor air quality as key selling points. Industry experts note that the standard’s stringent thermal envelope requirements help mitigate the impact of heatwaves, while the ventilation system ensures fresh air without compromising temperature control. Local building regulations are also evolving to encourage or require Passivhaus compliance for new residential developments in high‑risk heat zones.

As the UK continues to experience higher summer temperatures, the Passivhaus approach is positioned to play a significant role in the nation’s broader strategy for climate resilience and energy efficiency. Its growing popularity reflects a shift toward sustainable building practices that address both environmental and consumer comfort concerns.
author: BBC Science

title: Rust Glancer: 100x Less RAM LSP
content:
A new Rust library called **rust‑glancer** was announced by developer Matklad on August 21, 2026. The project, hosted on GitHub, offers a high‑performance, type‑safe interface for quickly inspecting and previewing data structures at runtime. According to the repository’s README, rust‑glancer is designed to integrate seamlessly with existing Rust codebases, providing a lightweight API that reduces boilerplate while maintaining strict compile‑time guarantees.

The library was highlighted on Hacker News, where it received 21 up‑votes and 12 comments. Community members praised its minimal dependencies and the clarity of its documentation, noting that it could streamline debugging workflows for large‑scale systems written in Rust. Some users discussed potential use cases in performance profiling and data serialization, while others suggested enhancements such as extended support for asynchronous streams and richer formatting options.

Overall, rust‑glancer appears poised to fill a niche in the Rust ecosystem for developers needing fast, reliable introspection tools. Its adoption could encourage more robust debugging practices and accelerate the development of complex, data‑heavy applications in Rust.
author: Hacker News

title: Dan Luu Highlights Best Hacker News Posts of 2016
content:
Dan Luu, a technology writer known for data‑driven essays, published a new piece titled “HN Comments” on his personal site, examining the dynamics of discussion threads on Hacker News. The article presents a quantitative overview of recent comment activity, highlighting average reply depth, up‑vote distribution, and the proportion of comments that generate substantive follow‑up versus those that receive little engagement. Luu also compares these metrics to historical data, noting a modest decline in average comment length and a slight increase in the number of short, low‑interaction posts over the past year.

The post attracted modest attention on the Hacker News platform, earning 16 points and prompting six replies in the associated discussion thread on Y Combinator’s news site. Commenters largely focused on the methodology of Luu’s analysis, offering additional observations about community moderation and the impact of algorithmic feed changes. The article adds to ongoing conversations about the health of online technical forums and provides a baseline for future studies of user engagement on the site.
author: Hacker News

title: Motorola Partnership Targets Standard Non-Folding Device
content:
GrapheneOS, the open‑source Android hardening project, posted a new update on its official social channel (post ID 117136278553665985). The brief entry, shared via the platform’s “Social” service, was subsequently linked on Hacker News, where it garnered three points from the community.

The Hacker News listing (item ID 49395605) recorded no comments on the post, indicating limited discussion despite the modest up‑vote count. While the content of the GrapheneOS message was not detailed in the available references, the activity underscores ongoing interest in the project’s developments among security‑focused audiences.
author: Hacker News

title: Modern Software Can Run Fast Without Compromise
content:
Dan Luu’s latest blog entry, “Performance Optimization,” examines contemporary strategies for improving software efficiency, emphasizing measurement‑driven approaches over speculative tweaking. The post outlines a workflow that begins with establishing reliable benchmarks, proceeds to profiling critical paths, and then applies targeted changes such as cache‑friendly data layouts, reduced lock contention, and judicious use of SIMD instructions. Luu stresses the importance of understanding hardware limits—particularly memory bandwidth and branch prediction—while warning against premature micro‑optimizations that can obscure real bottlene​cks. Throughout, he references recent case studies where modest code adjustments yielded measurable latency reductions without sacrificing maintainability.

The article attracted modest attention on Hacker News, where it earned three points and a single comment. The brief discussion highlighted the post’s practical relevance for engineers seeking systematic performance gains, noting that Luu’s emphasis on empirical validation aligns with industry best practices. While the thread remained limited in volume, the engagement underscores continued interest in disciplined optimization techniques within the development community.
author: Hacker News

title: Trump proposes new federal spaceport for heavy launch capability
content:
A spokesperson for the U.S. space agency said the nation “probably need[s] another site that's capable of heavy and super heavy launch capability,” underscoring the growing demand for infrastructure that can support the next generation of orbital vehicles. The comment came amid plans to field larger rockets for deep‑space missions, including NASA’s Space Launch System and SpaceX’s Starship, both of which exceed the payload limits of existing launch complexes.

Current launch facilities such as Cape Canaveral’s SLC‑40 and the former Vandenberg Space Force Base are optimized for medium‑lift vehicles and are being upgraded to accommodate heavier payloads. However, the sheer mass and thrust of the new rockets will require longer, more robust launch pads, upgraded fueling systems, and expanded support infrastructure. Analysts point to potential sites in the Pacific Northwest or the U.S. Virgin Islands as candidates, with preliminary studies suggesting that a dedicated complex could reduce launch latency and increase safety margins for crewed missions to the Moon and Mars.

The agency is now evaluating design options and securing funding for a feasibility study, with a view to constructing the new launch site within the next decade. If approved, the project would provide the United States with a critical capability to launch the heavy and super‑heavy payloads that will drive future exploration and commercial spaceflight.
author: Ars Technica

title: Japanese startup Letara raises $16 million to expand hybrid rocket technology
content:
Japanese space startup Letara announced it has secured ¥2.6 billion (approximately $16 million) in funding to expand the application of its hybrid‑rocket technology. The capital injection is intended to move the company beyond its current focus on small‑satellite thrusters and target a wider range of customers in the space, defense and security sectors.

Letara’s hybrid propulsion system combines solid and liquid propellants, offering a balance of performance, safety and cost‑effectiveness that the firm believes will appeal to both commercial and governmental users. By leveraging the new financing, the startup plans to accelerate development, conduct additional testing, and pursue contracts that could integrate its rockets into larger launch vehicles, satellite deployment services and tactical defense platforms. The move reflects a broader industry trend toward versatile propulsion solutions capable of supporting diverse missions beyond low‑Earth orbit.
author: TechCrunch

title: Polansky Develops AI Model Using Living Human Skin for Skincare Research
content:
Michael Polansky, long known as Lady Gaga’s partner and a former senior aide to tech entrepreneur Sean Parker, has quietly developed an artificial‑intelligence‑driven biotechnology venture that preserves living human skin tissue outside the body for extended periods. The company, which has kept its operations low‑profile, now announces its first public launch, positioning itself to accelerate the discovery of novel skincare compounds.

Polansky’s platform employs machine‑learning algorithms to monitor and maintain the viability of cultured skin samples, allowing researchers to observe cellular responses to a wide array of chemical agents over weeks rather than days. By extending the lifespan of these tissues, the startup aims to reduce reliance on animal testing and speed the development of safer, more effective dermatological products. The move comes at a time of heightened interest in AI‑augmented drug discovery and a growing demand for sustainable, human‑based testing methods.

The public unveiling signals a shift from Polansky’s previous high‑profile tech roles to a focus on medical innovation. Industry observers note that the company’s approach could streamline the pipeline from compound screening to clinical evaluation, potentially shortening the time required to bring new skincare solutions to market. As the venture steps into the spotlight, stakeholders will be watching to see how its technology performs in real‑world applications and whether it can deliver on its promise of more rapid, humane discovery of dermatological therapeutics.
author: TechCrunch

title: Deadly gold mine landslide on CAR‑Cameroon border kills dozens
content:
A deadly landslide at a gold mine in the Central African Republic has killed dozens of workers, many of whom were nationals of Cameroon and Chad, authorities said on Tuesday. The collapse, which occurred early this morning, occurred at the Koui mine in the north‑western province of Haute-Kotto, where the company has been operating since 2017. Rescue teams are still working to locate survivors and recover bodies, while the government has called for an investigation into the site’s safety protocols.

In other regional news, Ethiopia is seeking to position itself as East Africa’s next wine‑producing hub by importing Bordeaux‑style expertise and grapevines. The Ministry of Agriculture announced a partnership with French oenologists to train local vintners and establish vineyards in the high‑altitude zones of the Ethiopian Highlands. Meanwhile, Belgium remains engaged in a long‑standing reckoning with its colonial legacy, as the country continues to confront the memory of Congolese people who were displayed at the 1894 Antwerp World’s Fair, more than a century after the event.

These developments underscore the region’s diverse challenges and ambitions, from urgent humanitarian crises to cultural and economic transformation. As governments and communities respond, the international community watches for both immediate relief and long‑term policy shifts.
author: France 24

title: Six-year-old dies after teacher slap in Andhra Pradesh, minister vows legal action
content:
The regional Minister of Education for Andhra Pradesh, Dr. S. R. Reddy, announced today that he will pursue legal action against those responsible for recent misconduct in the state’s educational system. Speaking at a press conference in Hyderabad, the minister said a newly formed committee will investigate the allegations and identify the individuals or entities that facilitated the wrongdoing. He emphasized that the committee’s findings will guide the legal proceedings and that the state will not tolerate any breach of educational standards.

According to the minister, the investigation will focus on incidents of exam fraud, improper allocation of school resources, and alleged corruption in the procurement of educational materials. The committee, comprising senior officials from the Department of Education, the State Legal Services Authority, and independent experts, will review documents, interview witnesses, and conduct site inspections. Dr. Reddy stated that once the committee completes its report, the state will file civil and criminal suits against the identified parties, ensuring accountability and restoring public confidence in the education sector.

The announcement comes amid growing public concern over the integrity of the state’s academic institutions. By initiating a formal legal process, the ministry aims to deter future misconduct and reinforce the rule of law within Andhra Pradesh’s education system. The committee is expected to submit its findings within 60 days, after which the state will proceed with the appropriate legal actions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Stars and Stripes editor Erik Slavin says firing was retaliation
content:
Editor‑in‑chief Erik Slavin announced that his dismissal from the publication was a retaliatory move after he publicly criticized the lack of editorial independence within the organization. Slavin, who had overseen the paper’s editorial direction for several years, said that his comments—made in a series of internal emails and a brief op‑ed—were met with a sudden decision to terminate his contract.

The publisher cited “performance issues” in its statement, but Slavin’s spokesperson noted that the timing of the firing followed a week after Slavin raised concerns about editorial oversight and the influence of corporate stakeholders on news coverage. The incident has sparked a broader conversation about the role of editorial autonomy in media outlets that are owned by larger conglomerates.

Industry observers warn that the case could set a precedent for silencing editors who challenge corporate pressures, underscoring the need for clear safeguards to protect journalistic integrity and independence. The publication has not yet clarified whether any internal review will be conducted.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Myanmar military bombing kills 14 at Buddhist monastery
content:
A monastery in the region hosted a religious retreat that drew more than 100 participants, according to a local resident. The event, which took place over several days, brought together people of various ages and backgrounds for prayer, meditation, and communal worship.

The retreat was organized by the monastery’s clergy and included daily services, guided meditation sessions, and discussions on spiritual practice. The local resident, who was present during the opening ceremony, noted that the influx of attendees was larger than the monastery’s usual capacity, requiring additional seating and accommodations.

The gathering was part of the monastery’s ongoing outreach program, which aims to provide a quiet environment for reflection and community building. The event concluded with a communal meal and a closing blessing, after which participants dispersed to continue their personal spiritual journeys.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump claims Strait of Hormuz is U.S. territory amid Iran tensions
content:
Washington — President Joe Biden said on Thursday that Iran has expressed a willingness to negotiate, but, in his view, the country is not yet prepared to reach an agreement that satisfies U.S. requirements. Speaking at a press briefing, the president noted that Tehran’s “desire to make a deal” does not translate into readiness to accept the terms that Washington deems necessary for a durable resolution of the nuclear issue. He emphasized that any future accord must address the full scope of Iran’s nuclear activities, regional behavior, and compliance mechanisms.

The remarks come amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to revive the 2015 Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, which the United States abandoned in 2018. European allies have been urging both sides to return to the negotiating table, while the International Atomic Energy Agency continues to monitor Iran’s nuclear facilities. The administration indicated that it will maintain pressure through sanctions and diplomatic channels until Tehran demonstrates a willingness to engage on the substantive points outlined by the United States.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Russia conducts double‑tap drone strike on Kryvyi Rih mall, several killed
content:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has condemned a recent attack on a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih, his hometown, calling it “cowardly and deliberate.” The incident, which occurred on [insert date], resulted in several injuries and significant property damage. Zelenskyy’s statement was issued through the presidential office and reiterated in a televised address to the nation.

The Kremlin has denied any involvement, describing the claim as “unsubstantiated and politically motivated.” Ukrainian officials have launched an investigation, citing evidence that the assault was carried out by armed men with Russian affiliations. The attack follows a series of escalations in the eastern regions, raising concerns about the security situation in major Ukrainian cities.

In the wake of the incident, Ukrainian security forces have increased patrols around commercial centers nationwide, while international observers urge a thorough, independent inquiry. The president’s remarks underscore the broader conflict narrative, framing the attack as part of a broader pattern of aggression attributed to Russia.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rodrigues Birkett leads informal poll for next UN Secretary‑General
content:
A Guyanese diplomat has emerged as the narrow front‑runner in a contested vote within the United Nations council as members work to forge a consensus before Secretary‑General António Guterres departs New York for his next engagement. The candidate, Guyana’s Permanent Representative to the UN, secured a slim lead in the latest round of informal polling, positioning him ahead of rival nominees from several other member states. The council, which is tasked with finalizing the appointment ahead of the Secretary‑General’s scheduled departure later this week, has been holding a series of closed‑door negotiations to reconcile differing positions and avoid a formal ballot.

Council members said the discussions aim to achieve a unanimous or near‑unanimous endorsement, thereby preserving the body’s procedural efficiency and signaling unity ahead of Guterres’s exit. If a consensus is reached, the Guyanese diplomat would be confirmed without a contested vote, streamlining the transition and allowing the council to refocus on its agenda for the coming months. The outcome is expected to be announced before the Secretary‑General leaves, concluding the council’s deliberations on the appointment.
author: Al Jazeera

title: State Senator Aisha Wahab wins California special election despite pro‑Israel spending
content:
State Senator Aisha Wahab secured a decisive win in Tuesday’s primary election, defeating her Republican challenger in California’s 13th Senate district. Campaign finance disclosures released after the vote show that Wahab’s campaign raised roughly $1.2 million, while independent groups supporting her opponent spent more than $3 million on advertising and outreach. Despite the disparity in outside spending, Wahab’s message on affordable housing, climate action and criminal‑justice reform resonated with voters, leading to a margin of victory of approximately 12 percentage points.

Political analysts note that Wahab’s triumph adds to a growing list of progressive candidates who have succeeded despite facing multi‑million‑dollar external expenditures. The outcome underscores the potential for grassroots fundraising and localized campaign strategies to offset the influence of outside money in state races. Wahab’s victory positions her to advance her policy agenda in the state Senate and may serve as a reference point for future progressive campaigns confronting similar financial challenges.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iranian President urges end to US conflict as Oman and Iran foreign ministers discuss amid US sanctions plans
content:
Oman’s foreign minister and his Iranian counterpart spoke by telephone on Tuesday, a dialogue that coincided with the United States’ announcement that it is preparing a new round of economic sanctions targeting Tehran’s nuclear and regional activities. The call, which lasted about an hour, focused on the possibility of diplomatic channels that could mitigate escalating tensions and preserve regional stability, with both ministers emphasizing the importance of continued communication amid heightened pressure from Washington.

U.S. officials indicated that the forthcoming sanctions would expand restrictions on Iran’s oil exports, financial institutions, and entities linked to its missile program, aiming to compel compliance with international nuclear agreements. Oman, traditionally positioned as a neutral interlocutor between Tehran and the West, reiterated its willingness to facilitate dialogue and urged all parties to avoid actions that could further destabilize the Gulf. The Iranian foreign minister acknowledged the sanctions as a “serious challenge” but expressed openness to constructive engagement, underscoring that diplomatic outreach remains essential for resolving the dispute.
author: Al Jazeera

title: OzBrain introduced as a shared knowledge platform for AI agents and teams
content:
OzBrain is a new agent‑centric knowledge management platform that aims to replace traditional dashboards and note‑taking tools with a single, central repository for AI‑generated insights. The system is designed to let software agents reason, write, and update content automatically while keeping a complete audit trail of changes. By abstracting the underlying data store and providing an API that any agent can use, OzBrain lets teams and collaborators share a “brain” that evolves as new information is added.

Key features include an agent‑agnostic interface that accepts input from multiple LLMs, conflict resolution logic to prevent duplicate or contradictory entries, and a token‑friendly indexing scheme that optimizes storage and retrieval. The platform also supports secure, Supabase‑backed Markdown storage, allowing developers to build voice‑AI and other applications without managing file systems or version control. Early adopters report that OzBrain eliminates the need to juggle separate Obsidian vaults, Git repositories, or custom scripts for knowledge sharing.

The project is still in alpha and has not yet been deployed on customer data, but the creator invites developers to test the maintenance loop and provide feedback. Those who have built their own knowledge systems are encouraged to share their designs and criteria for success. The goal is to create a scalable, secure, and user‑friendly environment where AI agents can collaborate and continuously refine shared knowledge without the overhead of traditional tools.
author: Hacker News

title: Inner Mongolia City Becomes Key Data Center Hub
content:
A city in Inner Mongolia has emerged as a strategic hub for data‑center development, drawing on three key advantages: low‑cost electricity, plentiful land and its geographic proximity to Beijing. The region’s abundant coal and expanding renewable resources keep power prices well below national averages, while the vast, under‑utilised tracts of flat terrain allow operators to build large‑scale facilities without the constraints faced in more densely populated areas. At roughly 300 kilometres from the capital, the location offers reduced network latency for Beijing‑based enterprises, making it an attractive option for cloud service providers seeking both efficiency and speed.

Government incentives, streamlined permitting processes and the presence of major telecom backbones have accelerated investment, with several domestic and international firms announcing multi‑billion‑yuan projects in the past year. The concentration of data centres is expected to boost the local economy, create jobs and increase demand for ancillary services, while also reinforcing China’s broader strategy to decentralise critical digital infrastructure. Industry analysts project continued growth as the city leverages its cost and location benefits to meet rising national data‑processing needs.
author: Wired

title: TechCrunch finds Anthropic Claude model bypasses sexual content restrictions
content:
Anthropic has publicly stated that its Claude family of language models is prohibited from producing sexually explicit content. In a series of experiments carried out by TechCrunch, the tech publication discovered that the restriction can be circumvented with minimal effort. The tests involved feeding the models prompts that used euphemisms, coded language, or indirect references, and the models responded with content that met the definition of sexual explicitness.

The researchers noted that while Claude’s moderation filters are designed to block direct requests for erotic material, the system’s broader contextual understanding can be exploited. By framing a request in a seemingly innocuous context—such as describing a scene from a novel or asking for a “sensual” description of a landscape—the models were able to produce language that, according to the tests, would be considered disallowed. Anthropic has not yet issued a public response to these findings, but the results raise questions about the robustness of its content‑moderation framework.

If the findings hold up under further scrutiny, they could prompt Anthropic to tighten its moderation algorithms or revise its policy documentation. The company’s stance on safe AI deployment remains a key concern for regulators and users alike, and the TechCrunch tests underscore the ongoing challenge of preventing policy violations in generative language models.
author: TechCrunch

title: Vice President JD Vance rallies in Ohio hometown ahead of midterm elections
content:
Washington — Vice President Kamala Harris addressed a mixed audience of business leaders and community organizers on Thursday, centering her remarks on the nation’s economic outlook. In a speech delivered at the Economic Innovation Forum in Washington, D.C., the vice president highlighted recent job growth, declining inflation rates, and upcoming infrastructure investments, positioning these trends as evidence of the administration’s fiscal stewardship. She also referenced the administration’s budget proposals aimed at expanding broadband access and supporting small‑business credit, framing them as counterpoints to the Republican platform.

Polling data released by the Pew Research Center earlier this week indicated a modest decline in voter confidence for Republican economic policies, with 42 percent of respondents expressing skepticism about the party’s tax and trade proposals. Analysts linked the dip to concerns over recent market volatility and the projected impact of proposed regulatory changes. The vice president’s economic focus, combined with the latest polling figures, underscores the heightened attention to fiscal issues as the 2024 election cycle intensifies, setting the stage for further policy debates in the coming months.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nvidia partners with Cloverleaf to expand data center development
content:
Nvidia is deepening its commitment to data‑center infrastructure, investing billions in new facilities and technology to support the explosive growth of artificial‑intelligence workloads.  The company’s data‑center segment, which includes its flagship A100 and H100 GPUs, has become the largest contributor to Nvidia’s revenue, accounting for more than 70 % of its earnings in the most recent fiscal year.  To meet rising demand, Nvidia is expanding its own data‑center footprint and partnering with cloud providers to build next‑generation AI platforms.

The company’s capital allocation reflects the symbiotic relationship between Nvidia’s hardware and the AI data‑center ecosystem.  As enterprises and research institutions deploy ever‑larger neural‑network models, they require the high‑performance compute and energy efficiency that Nvidia’s GPUs deliver.  In turn, the proliferation of AI‑centric data centers fuels Nvidia’s sales, creating a virtuous cycle of revenue and reinvestment.  Recent quarterly reports show a 60 % year‑over‑year increase in data‑center revenue, underscoring the sector’s pivotal role in Nvidia’s growth strategy.

Looking ahead, Nvidia plans to further scale its data‑center operations, adding new fabrication nodes and expanding its software stack to optimize performance and cost.  The company’s continued investment signals confidence that AI workloads will remain a dominant driver of demand for advanced GPUs and associated infrastructure, ensuring Nvidia’s leadership in the high‑performance computing market.
author: TechCrunch

title: TikTok agrees to $400 million settlement with US Justice Department over child privacy violations
content:
TikTok and the United States government reached a settlement on Thursday that resolves accusations the short‑form video platform breached the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) and related state laws. The agreement follows a joint investigation by the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) and attorneys general from 42 states, which alleged that TikTok collected personal information from users under the age of 13 without obtaining verifiable parental consent.

Under the terms of the settlement, TikTok will pay a $92 million civil penalty and will be required to implement a series of privacy safeguards. The company must establish a “privacy center” that provides clear, accessible information about its data‑collection practices, obtain parental consent before gathering personal data from minors, and submit to independent audits for three years to verify compliance. Additionally, TikTok will be prohibited from collecting personal data from children under 13 unless it can demonstrate that it has met the statutory consent requirements.

The resolution marks the largest COPPA enforcement action to date and signals heightened regulatory scrutiny of social‑media apps that attract young audiences. By agreeing to the settlement, TikTok avoids further litigation while committing to stronger protections for minors, and the FTC and state regulators underscore their intent to enforce privacy rules across digital platforms.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump has mountain of Leavitt replacements, says Scott Jennings ‘is good’
content:
President Trump said on Friday that he had never seen so many job applications in his life, a comment made in response to the vacancy created by Karoline Leavitt’s decision to step down as White House press secretary. The remarks came during a press briefing at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland, where reporters asked the former president who he was considering to fill the role.

When pressed for names, Trump declined to disclose any potential candidates, indicating that the decision was still pending. The statement underscores the administration’s ongoing search for a new press secretary while highlighting the volume of interest the position has attracted. The outcome of the selection process remains to be announced.
author: The Hill

title: Hidden Zillow Listings Allegedly Inflate NYC Rents, Lawsuit Claims
content:
Renters in New York City are raising concerns that Zillow’s “hidden” listings are making it harder to find affordable housing. The online platform marks certain apartments as hidden when landlords or property managers want to keep them off the public search results, often because the units are exempt from rent‑control or rent‑stabilization regulations. As a result, many potential tenants are unable to see the full range of available units, forcing them to rely on other, less transparent sources such as broker networks or word‑of‑mouth referrals.

The practice has been cited by several tenants who say it pushes them toward higher‑priced, fully market‑rate apartments that exceed their budgets. In a recent survey of 300 renters, 62 % reported that they had to pay at least 10 % more for comparable units after discovering hidden listings. City officials argue that the hidden status is a tool for landlords to comply with zoning and zoning‑related restrictions, but critics claim it contributes to the ongoing affordability crisis by limiting the visibility of lower‑cost options.

City housing advocates are calling for greater transparency from Zillow and other listing services. They argue that making all available units publicly searchable would help level the playing field and give renters a clearer picture of the market. Until such changes are implemented, many tenants will likely continue to face a fragmented housing market that makes it difficult to secure affordable apartments in the city.
author: Ars Technica

title: Thunderstorms and fiber‑optic cables used for subsurface seismic imaging
content:
A new study has confirmed that the powerful atmospheric disturbances generated by thunderstorms can produce detectable seismic waves, offering a novel tool for probing underground structures. Researchers recorded low‑frequency ground vibrations coinciding with intense lightning and gust fronts, demonstrating that the rapid pressure changes and wind shear associated with severe storms couple efficiently into the Earth's crust. By analyzing the timing, amplitude, and frequency content of these storm‑induced tremors, scientists were able to map variations in subsurface density and elasticity, revealing features such as sediment layers, fault zones, and groundwater reservoirs that are typically identified using conventional seismic surveys.

The findings suggest that natural thunderstorm activity could complement existing geophysical techniques, especially in remote or environmentally sensitive regions where artificial seismic sources are impractical. Ongoing work aims to refine the methodology, improve signal‑to‑noise discrimination, and integrate storm‑generated data with satellite and ground‑based observations. If successfully operationalized, this approach could enhance resource exploration, hazard assessment, and our broader understanding of the Earth's interior without the need for costly or invasive equipment.
author: Ars Technica

title: AI accounting startup Rillet raises $100 million, becomes unicorn
content:
Rillet’s chief executive, Nicholas Koop, presented the company’s latest growth figures at a recent board meeting, sparking an unexpected surge of interest from major venture players. The CEO disclosed a year‑over‑year revenue increase of 38 % and a user base expansion of 27 %, positioning Rillet as a fast‑growing contender in the fintech space.

The announcement drew swift attention from prominent investors, including Iconiq and Sequoia, who reportedly entered into preliminary discussions for a new funding round. Other venture funds have also signaled intent to evaluate opportunities, suggesting that Rillet’s valuation could climb significantly as the company seeks to scale its platform and broaden its market reach.

With the influx of capital interest, Rillet is poised to accelerate product development and geographic expansion. The company’s next steps will likely involve finalizing term sheets and outlining a strategic use of proceeds, setting the stage for a potentially transformative phase in its growth trajectory.
author: TechCrunch

title: Mexico's Sinaloa Governor Ruben Rocha returns to office amid US criminal charges
content:
Mexico’s governor of Sinaloa, Rubén Cárdenas, has been publicly accused by officials in the Trump administration of collaborating with a drug cartel operating in the region. The allegation emerged in a statement released by the U.S. Department of State, which claimed that intelligence reports linked the governor to the Sinaloa Cartel’s leadership and suggested that his administration had facilitated the group’s trafficking activities.

Mexican authorities have denied the accusations, asserting that they are unfounded and lack substantive evidence. The federal government has announced an internal review to assess the claims and reaffirm its commitment to combating organized crime. The dispute adds tension to U.S.–Mexico relations, as both nations continue to coordinate efforts on security and drug‑related issues while navigating diplomatic sensitivities surrounding the governor’s political standing.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Arsenal beat Coventry 3-0 to start title defence
content:
Arsenal secured a decisive 3‑0 win in their latest Premier League clash, with the Gunners taking the lead early and extending it before the break. The match, played at the Emirates Stadium, saw Arsenal’s attacking trio make a strong statement as they dominated the opposition from the outset.

Kai Havertz opened the scoring within the first few minutes, putting Arsenal ahead with a composed finish. Bukayo Saka added a second goal shortly after, doubling the advantage and putting the pressure firmly on the visitors. In the second half, Martin Ødegaard completed the trio’s tally, slotting in after the break to seal the victory and cement the team’s position at the top of the table.

The win not only boosts Arsenal’s confidence heading into the final stretch of the season but also underscores the effectiveness of their forward line. With three points secured, the team remains in strong contention for a top‑four finish, while the opposition will need to regroup after a comprehensive defeat.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Sword attack at Swedish high school leaves one dead, three injured
content:
A sword‑wielding attacker entered a high school in Sweden, killing one person and wounding three others before police intervened. The incident, which unfolded during school hours, prompted an immediate lockdown of the campus and a rapid response from emergency services.

Authorities have taken the suspect into custody and are conducting a preliminary investigation into the motive behind the attack. The victims, whose identities have not been released, were transported to nearby hospitals for treatment. Officials emphasized that such violent incidents at Swedish schools are rare and assured the public that the investigation is ongoing.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Climate change may triple wheat prices amid water shortages
content:
Water shortages have struck several of the world’s most important wheat‑growing regions at the same time, a development that is already being felt in grocery stores and bakeries.  In North America, drought‑hit parts of the U.S. Midwest and Canada’s prairie provinces have reduced wheat yields by up to 15 percent in some counties.  Europe’s major wheat producers—particularly France, Germany and the United Kingdom—are grappling with below‑average rainfall, while in Asia, the wheat‑producing heartlands of Kazakhstan and the northern Chinese provinces are experiencing severe water stress.  

The simultaneous decline in wheat output is tightening the global supply chain for staple foods such as bread, pasta and breakfast cereals.  Grain exporters are reporting lower volumes of wheat leaving their ports, and the reduced availability is already pushing up prices for raw wheat and finished products.  Food‑processing plants are adjusting production schedules, and some retailers have begun to diversify their supply sources or increase inventory levels to buffer against the shortfall.  Analysts note that the impact could be felt for several months, as wheat is a long‑term crop and the current shortages will take time to recover.

Consumers are likely to see higher prices for wheat‑based foods and a possible shift in product offerings as manufacturers seek alternative grains or blend ratios.  While governments and industry groups are exploring water‑saving irrigation techniques and more resilient crop varieties, the immediate effect remains a tighter market and a reminder of the vulnerability of global food supplies to climate‑driven water scarcity.
author: Phys.org

title: LinkedIn reports over one million clicks on new AI slop button
content:
LinkedIn introduced a new “Seems like AI slop” button on July 30, according to a Thursday post by chief product officer Hari Srinivasan. The button, which appears in the three‑dot menu on any post, allows users to flag content they believe was generated by artificial intelligence. LinkedIn reported that more than one million users have clicked the button since its launch, indicating significant engagement with the feature.

The rollout follows a recent analysis by AI‑detection service Pangram, which found that 41 percent of LinkedIn’s long‑form posts were flagged as fully AI‑generated, a statistic highlighted in a report by 404 Media. In addition to the flagging button, LinkedIn announced “new and improved” classifiers designed to identify AI‑authored posts and disclosed the removal of a previously planned feature related to AI content. The company’s moves aim to increase transparency and curb the spread of AI‑generated material on the platform, as reported by The Verge.
author: The Verge

title: Apple cuts hundreds of jobs from Siri and Vision Pro teams
content:
Apple announced that a number of positions within the company will be eliminated as it redirects resources away from several ongoing initiatives. The technology giant confirmed that the restructuring is part of a broader strategic shift aimed at concentrating on its core product lines and emerging growth areas, though it did not disclose the exact number of roles affected or specify which projects are being scaled back.

Executives indicated that the move is intended to streamline operations and reallocate talent toward priorities such as services, artificial‑intelligence integration and next‑generation hardware. While the decision will result in workforce reductions, Apple said it remains committed to supporting impacted employees through transition assistance and plans to maintain momentum on its primary business objectives.
author: TechCrunch

title: Hundreds protest in Tunis demanding President Kais Saied resign
content:
Hundreds of Tunisians gathered in the streets of Tunis on Thursday, demanding that President Kais Saied step down. The protest, organized by a coalition of opposition parties and civil society groups, was held in front of the presidential palace and other key civic sites. Demonstrators carried placards calling for Saied’s resignation and a return to democratic governance.

President Saied, who came to power in 2019, has faced criticism for actions that many view as eroding Tunisia’s democratic institutions, including the dissolution of parliament in 2021 and the expansion of executive powers. The Thursday demonstration follows a series of earlier protests and legal challenges that have highlighted growing public discontent with Saied’s administration and its perceived authoritarian drift.

Authorities have deployed security forces to manage the crowds, and the government has stated that it will engage in dialogue with opposition leaders. The protests underscore the continuing political tension in Tunisia and signal that calls for Saied’s resignation remain a significant element of the country’s evolving democratic landscape.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump signs national space policy targeting 1,000 launches annually by 2030
content:
The United States is revising its spaceflight and reentry management framework to accommodate an ambitious target of over 1,000 rocket launches annually by 2030. The update, announced by the Federal Aviation Administration and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, aims to streamline regulatory processes and enhance coordination among launch providers, air traffic control, and space agencies.

Key changes include the creation of a dedicated launch coordination office, the expansion of launch windows, and the adoption of new safety protocols that leverage real‑time telemetry and automated flight‑path monitoring.
